News.title: Newquay deaths: Dad and daughter die at Britain's top surfing spot as police search for handbag
News.content:
Beachgoers bravely tried to rescue a man and woman after they reportedly fell from rocks and died in the choppy sea at Britain's most popular surfing spot.

Police have urged the public to be on the lookout for an orange handbag containing items of 'great sentimental value' after a father and his daughter, in their 60s and 30s, died tragically at Britain's most famous surfing beach in Cornwall.

People at Fistral Beach, in Newquay, bravely attempted to rescue the pair after they fell from some rocks into water below on Sunday evening, with nine emergency vehicles and a helicopter rushing to the 750-metre long sands, known as the 'home of British surfing' , to assist in the doomed rescue effort.

The area is well-known for having extremely strong and dangerous rip currents, particularly during outgoing tides. Locals said the sea currents were "very strong" last night.

Following news of their deaths, police urged the public to look for a "leather-style" handbag approximately 30cm by 30cm in size worn by the woman at the time of her death. The bag, described as "orange or peach in colour", is said to contain a number of sentimental items that grieving family members "would take great comfort in being reunited with," police said in a statement.

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: Xbox down as frustrated gamers can't sign in after system hit by global outage
News.content:
Xbox users have reported a series of issues with the gaming platform on Downdetector. The problem appears to be global and there are hundreds of cases in the UK alone

Xbox down as frustrated gamers can't sign in after system hit by global outage

Gamers are reporting a a major global outage with Xbox with frustrated players saying they are unable to sign in.

Hundreds of users have taken to Downdetector, which reports online outages, to report issues with launching games and server connections.

Xbox Support issued a message earlier today, saying they were aware some users were encountering errors when "attempting to sign in, see your game library or launch games".

In their latest update, they said: "Just checking in on the game library, sign-in, and game launch issue. We know this has been going on a while and appreciate your patience while our teams keep working on it. "

News.title: Dramatic moment smoke column amid France wildfires becomes thunderstorm
News.content:
A monster wildfire tearing through southwest France grew so powerful that its smoke column became a thunderstorm - generating lightning which ignited a slew of new fires.

Apocalyptic new images taken following the outbreak of a fire near Saumos, in France's Gironde department, show a terrifying wall of smoke stretching into the sky for miles. The now 162-square mile blaze ignited on July 22, and has rapidly eaten away at the community.

Like many others that have formed in the nation and its neighbour Spain over the last two weeks, it has forced people to flee for safety, with 240 homes abandoned and 220,000 people evacuated so far.

The Saumos fire is notably different from its fellow fires, however, as it has become dangerously self-sustaining. According to scientists, it has prompted a phenomenon named the pyrocumulonimbus - which typically are only able to develop in the most extreme environments.

‌



Met Office shows when temperatures peak in new heatwave as 20 areas face 30C or more READ MORE :

Emmanuel Macron says France wildfires are nation's biggest crisis since Second World War READ MORE :

View 4 Images The pyrocumulonimbus has been raining lightning that has caused new fires (Image: AP Photo/Caroline Blumberg)

A pyrocumulonimbus, otherwise known as pyroCb, is rare in Europe, as they tend to spawn in the generally more extreme conditions seen in North America and Australia. Even there, the fire-fuelled storm clouds are only created in the most intense fires. They have never before been encountered by firefighters in France, according to the country's national firefighters federation.

The departmental fire and rescue service said it had generated a pyrocumulonimbus just two days after spawning, with heat and smoke surging upward into a vast black, electrified thundercloud.

Theodore Giannaros, a fire meteorologist at the National Observatory of Athens, explained the firestorms are generated by a mix of extreme heat, smoke and moisture. He said: "Imagine a campfire so large and hot that the smoke rising off it turns into a storm-like cloud. That is a pyroCb — a storm cloud born from the intense heat that a wildfire produces."

‌



View 4 Images PyroCBs only usually develop in the most extreme of environments (Image: AP Photo/Emma Da Silva)

Pyrocumulonimbus do not form at a set temperature, instead requiring very hot, very dry air near the ground, with cooler and moister air above it.

Hot air loaded with smoke and moisture then rises rapidly from the flames. As it climbs and cools, water vapor condenses around particles of ash. Above the freezing level, droplets become ice crystals whose collisions separate electrical charges, as in an ordinary thunderstorm.

Mr Giannaros added:“It’s a feedback loop, not a one-way effect. Once it forms, the cloud becomes its own weather system, sitting on top of the fire and making it harder to predict.” The systems can also spin up whirling columns of flame — usually a fire whirl, which Giannaros describes as a dust devil made of fire and heat instead of dust.

‌



View 4 Images The situation is only expected to get worse in the days to come (Image: AP Photo/Caroline Blumberg)

In Europe, pyroCbs have been rare, with Portugal recording one during its deadly 2017 fire season. France has now joined the list as the nation's wildfire crisis only deepens.

The fires are only expected to get worse in the days to come, with a looming 40C heatwave making more wildfires likely and creating even more difficulty for firefighters tackling existing blazes. Around 300,000 people have been displaced in the last week alone, and the country's president, Emmanuel Macron, has said the crisis is the worst France has faced since World War Two.

Macron said the Gironde blaze was "unprecedented", during a visit to the departmental fire and rescue operational centre (CODIS) in blaze-hit Bordeaux, adding: "The weeks ahead will be difficult and we must hold on."

News.title: France wildfires live: Inferno is country's 'most difficult situation since WW2' - Macron
News.content:
More than 220,000 people in south-west France's Gironde region have been evacuated as raging wildfires approach Bordeaux

French President Emmanuel Macron has claimed the raging wildfires are the 'most difficult situation' his country has dealt with since World War Two.

Fierce wildfires are currently burning seven miles from the French city of Bordeaux and its airport, with more than 220,000 people evacuated from their homes in the south-west of the country.

Firefighters are struggling to contain the flames, which have burned 42,000 hectares - an area four times the size of Paris - leaving two firefighters dead and 88 injured. Volunteers, including local farmers, are helping by towing huge water tankers to the scene.

France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez says the 'unprecedented' wildfires have developed a "life of their own," while Bordeaux's mayor has labelled the blaze the "fire of the century" that could take months to extinguish.

Meanwhile in Spain, 25,000 people have been ordered to evacuate and almost 40,000 have been told to stay indoors. Wildfires near Madrid "slowed their advance" overnight but remain active, the regional government said today.

News.title: Lloyds and Barclays down: Hundreds 'can't make payments' as Halifax also hit
News.content:
Lloyds, Barclays and Halifax customers all experienced issues for several hours today, including problems with the app, bank transfers and online banking

Lloyds and Barclays down: Hundreds 'can't make payments' as Halifax also hit

Lloyds, Barclays and Halifax customers reported major problems with their banking this afternoon.

Customers said they were unable to make payments or transfer money, while others received messages warning them payment had failed but later realised the money had actually gone through.

Lloyds Bank said it was investigating an issue affecting Faster Payments, which "may cause delays".

The bank also urged customers who have attempted to send money not to send it again as this may result in duplicate payments.

Hundreds of Barclays customers said they had been unable to receive external payments, while the majority of Halifax users reporting issues today said they were struggling to transfer funds.

News.title: Huge shake-up to education system for 14-year-olds lined up by Andy Burnham
News.content:
Huge shake-up to education system for 14-year-olds lined up by Andy Burnham

The changes come as the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham seeks to tackle the one million young people not in employment, education or training - or ‘Neets’

View 3 Images Pupils at a school in Glasgow interact during a biology class (file image) (Image: Getty Images)

New technical education routes will be available to 14-year-olds as Andy Burnham drives reforms to tackle youth unemployment.

‌



The new Prime Minister said he wants there to be “no dead ends” for young people coming out of education, and for technical pathways to be put on an equal footing with traditional academic routes.

‌



From Year 10, pupils will be able to combine core academic subjects, like English and Maths, with technical education linked to jobs available in their area. Mr Burnham is expected to tell students on Tuesday: "Whether you choose construction, coding or classics, you’ll get the skills you need and be given the respect you deserve."

‌



Downing Street said Mr Burnham will launch “new prestigious technical education routes”. It is part of measures Mr Burnham is expected to introduce to tackle "Neets" - young people not in employment, education or training, of which there are more than one million in the UK.

The new scheme will be devised with regional mayors, local leaders, and schools, No10 added.

The announcement on Tuesday builds on his flagship education policy as Greater Manchester mayor. During his tenure the Greater Manchester Baccalaureate (MBacc) was launched in an attempt to put technical education on an equal footing with traditional academic routes.

‌



It also offers students a significant work experience placement.

More than 1million young people not in work or education as 'snowflake' myths blasted READ MORE :

View 3 Images Former Cabinet minister Alan Milburn sounded the alarm about the crisis in May (Image: Jeff Moore/PA Wire)

The PM said: “For too long in this country, students have been told that you must take the academic path to do well and to be respected. The whole school system has been built around it and that has let down young people seeking technical qualifications.

‌



“I want an education system based on parity between academic and technical which gives all young people a clear path in life. From today, Britain will value the hard hat every bit as much as the graduation cap.”

He added: “Fixing the youth unemployment crisis in Britain will require a major shake-up in how we do things – and that’s what this government will do.

“I want to ensure that our education system leaves no dead ends for our young people. The changes we’re announcing today will just be the start of our work to restore opportunity and hope across the country.”

‌



It follows a major report earlier this year by the former Labour Cabinet minister Alan Milburn warned that without action on the issue there could be a £125billion hit to the economy. He is set to publish his recommendations on tackling the crisis in the autumn.

Mr Milburn welcomed the latest measures, saying: “A million young people are being failed by a system that isn’t creating the opportunities for them to progress in life.

"The world of work is changing and the education system isn’t keeping up. The changes the PM is announcing today are very welcome. They are a big step in the right direction and consistent with the findings of my review.

‌



“A whole system reset is needed across health, welfare and labour market policy as well as in education and skills. I know the PM recognises this and my final report will outline the further changes that are needed.”

View 3 Images Andy Burnham has said young people should not be blamed for a lack of support (Image: AP Photo/Kirsty Wigglesworth)

It comes after Mr Burnham used an interview with BBC Panorama to warn that young people have been let down by an education system “obsessed” with the university route. He said young people in their twenties were not to blame and had been “seriously let down because the support wasn’t there”.

‌



He said: “I’m talking about a school system that doesn’t have the right support for young people with special educational needs, or disabilities.

“I’m talking about an education system that for a very long time has been obsessed on the university route - but hasn’t done enough for young people who want technical qualifications and in many ways has treated them as second class students.”

He added: “That all leaves people when they get to their late teenage years in the position where they don’t know where life is taking them - so I don’t blame them. I don’t think the support has been there for them in the way it should have been.”

Article continues below

Mr Burnham also suggested it should be harder for people - particularly youngsters - to be able to claim benefits. He indicated he plans to "increase the conditions on people required to receive benefits”.

He said: "It's about changing the nature of the support and making some of the support conditional upon people taking opportunities that are presented in front of them. So you might increase the conditions required to receive benefits."

News.title: Iran shares chilling video explaining 'where and how' to kill Melania Trump
News.content:
Iran shares chilling video explaining 'where and how' to kill Melania Trump

A video has emerged where a narrator speaking Farsi talks about 'how and where' to kill Melania Trump which comes as the Iranian regime has threatened revenge on the US President

View 3 Images A chilling Iranian video offers instructions on how to kill Melania Trump (Image: https://x.com/sabra_the)

Both Melania Trump and her son Barron have been targeted by the Iranian regime in a chilling new video that provides detailed instructions explaining 'how and where' to kill the First Lady.

‌



The video, released by IRGC-affiliated news agency Tasnim, depicts a Farsi-speaking narrator outlining and encouraging various potential assassination 'plots' against Melania, before threatening Barron Trump and telling him to "wait for us."

‌



Highlighting Melania's "love of fashion" as her biggest weakness while showing pictures of her in her motorcade and highlighting her favourite designer stores, the narrator suggests a potential poisoning scheme that can be carried out by "freedom fighters" with access to areas the First Lady often visits.

‌



View 3 Images Iran has made threats against Trump and his family (Image: Jim LoScalzo - Pool via CNP/Shutterstock)

Andy Burnham rules out scrapping stamp duty but makes fairer taxation pledge READ MORE :

Such locations could be “suitable for operations by global freedom fighters,” the video noted, while suggesting that any potential assassins could use a nerve agent to poison any clothes the first lady might purchase.

At the start of the video, the narrator says that "the documents used in this video are the result of extracting information from several anonymous security networks and satellite images," although most of the information contained is about Melania's habits, mostly public information.

‌



At the end of the video it also stated: "Barron, wait for us."

It comes as Barron Trump was also featured in a disturbing display on a billboard in Iran with Donald Trump's daughter Ivanka and Melania.

View 3 Images Barron Trump has also been targeted by Iran (Image: AP)

‌



All three were depicted with their eyes closed, with the word "KILLED" written in red across the top. "Hey, Terrorist! Get ready to die," read text placed next to the photographs.

Since the US and Israeli raids on Iran at the end of February that killed the late Supreme Leader, the regime has vowed revenge against Donald Trump.

And earlier this month Trump posted on his social media website that Iran had made threats “to assassinate, or attempt to assassinate” him, adding that 1,000 “missiles are Locked and Loaded and aimed at the Islamic Republic of Iran, with thousands more to immediately follow, should the Iranian Government act on its threat.”

Article continues below

Hours later Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, said that Iranians would continue to avenge the killing of his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The elder Khamenei has been mourned in funeral events throughout Iran earlier this month. His son said retaliation “is the will of our nation and must certainly be carried out.”

Another billboard this week in Iran showed a red MAGA hat with what appears to be an illustration of Trump with blood streaming from his head.

While a further has AI-generated imagery of Trump, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio drowning in a pool of blood.

News.title: Ex-Olympic swimming coach branded a 'monster' and 'serial paedophile' by victims in court
News.content:
Ex-Olympic swimming coach branded a 'monster' and 'serial paedophile' by victims in court

Former Irish Olympic swimming coach George Gibney was labelled a 'monster' by his victims after being found guilty of sexually abusing four girls over 50 years ago

View 4 Images Former Irish swimming coach George Gibney pictured in 1988

Convicted child abuser George Gibney's victims have branded him a "monster" who abused his position as a swimming coach to prey on young women, a Dublin court has heard.

The former Irish Olympic swimming coach was found guilty of indecently assaulting four girls, as well as the attempted rape of one of the girls in a changing room when she was 12.

Harrowing victim impact statements read at Dublin's Central Criminal Court today heard how the abuse was a secret one woman "carried in silence for years" as she watched Gibney being "lauded" and "hero-worshipped".

Another victim said the legal process had been "traumatic," with media reporting of the case being overly graphic.

She said she was relieved she never spoke to a counsellor about her ordeal as a request was made for notes from such sessions to be used as part of the trial.

Gibney, 78, pleaded guilty to five charges of indecently assaulting a girl in Ireland in 1976, but denied dozens of other charges of indecently assaulting the girls when they were aged between eight and 14, at various locations between 1971 and 1981.

Earlier this month, the jury returned guilty verdicts on 40 charges relating to incidents in the 1970s and 1980s.

A lawyer for Gibney confirmed in court today that he would not be appealing against his convictions.

View 4 Images Victim impact statements were read at the Criminal Courts of Justice in Dublin (Image: Collins Photo Agency)

The barrister said Gibney's reputation was "entirely in tatters", that he was not in the best health and that he "never receives visits" in prison, as a consequence of his actions.

He added that Gibney "accepts the verdicts of the jury".

Delivering their victim impact statements in court, three of the women thanked the gardaí for supporting and listening to them.

One woman turned to face Gibney in the witness box and said she went to the gardaí as she wanted "an official record of your evilness".

She said his assault of her was a "secret I carried in silence for years" as she watched him being "lauded" and "hero-worshipped" as she struggled.

Gibney held one of his hands in the other and looked ahead as she spoke.

She said she had no expectation when she first went to gardaí that charges would be filed, and that it was a "liberation of years of secrets" to tell the "truth of your degenerate behaviour".

She said even though Gibney had tried to destroy her as a child, "the world will now know you as a convicted, serial paedophile".

View 4 Images Gibney, a former Olympic swimming coach, was found guilty of indecently assaulting four girls (Image: Unknown)

The victim added that the cross examination was "exhausting", as she found it "distressing" to have to explain how he had controlled her, but that the guilty verdicts were "so overwhelmingly powerful, I cried".

Another woman said the court process was "exceedingly traumatic and lengthy" and that she had been told that she was "a witness for the state".

She said this conveyed to her the "lack of empathy or understanding" for victims in the legal process. "I am a victim first and a witness for the state second," she told the court.

‌



The victim said she had held the "deep dark secret within" and did not know counselling existed years ago.

She said during the trial process, any counselling notes from sessions she had were sought, and "thankfully, I had none" as she feared she would be subjected to "further humiliation".

She added: "I feel angry, so angry" and retraumatised by the court process. The woman said the abuse had also affected her relationships.

‌



She also criticised those who were "licking their chops salaciously" at the "blow by blow coverage" - and praised members of the media who reported it without the graphic detail.

She also questioned who she would have been "had this manipulator not violated me" at a time when "Catholic Ireland" swept abuse "under the mat" and left victims to "fend for themselves".

View 4 Images Gibney was also found guilty of 40 charges relating to incidents in the 1970s and 1980s.

‌



The woman told the court Gibney's abuse was even "hitting me in the wallet" as she explained she did not get paid if she missed work, but wanted to be in court for as much of the trial as she could.

A third victim said she was left "emotionally battered" and "humiliated" by Gibney, the press, and by a legal system "in need of reform".

Another victim, who said she remembers Gibney's car headlights at the roundabout as he came to collect her, said she "didn't feel like prey then but does now" as she recalled the memory.

‌



She said she had nightmares about Gibney during the pandemic and smoked heavily, and that when she went to gardaí, she was not being "courageous as reported in the media, I was desperate".

She added: "If it weren't for the Gardaí and my children, I don't know where I'd be."

She said the gardaí had "made me feel safe for the first time in my life" despite the process of giving evidence being "gruelling".

Article continues below

Gibney's lawyer told the court that his client had no previous convictions before this trial.

"In my respectful position, the person who is before you is a very different person than the person who committed these offences against young children who were in his care," he said.

Gibney is due to be sentenced on October 12.

News.title: Devastating European wildfires in maps - and how they're being tackled
News.content:
Wildfires are tearing through France and Spain, forcing more than 300,000 people to evacuate their homes.

France has seen its worst fires in two decades, while officials in the Spanish capital Madrid say they are the worst the region has ever experienced.

It follows a sweltering summer of heatwaves across Europe that have seen temperatures soar above 40C (104F) in many places.

Separate wildfires in the regions outside Madrid have together burned about 297 sq miles (770 sq km), authorities estimate - an area larger than Madrid itself.

News.title: Funeral director who left people unburied breached families' trust 'on industrial scale', court hears
News.content:
A funeral director who failed to bury people and gave out wrong ashes has breached the trust of bereaved families "on an almost industrial scale", a court has heard.

Some 35 bodies and more than 100 sets of ashes were found by police raiding Legacy Independent Funeral Directors in Hull in March 2024.

Owner Robert Bush previously admitted 67 offences, including 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial, and theft from 12 charities.

At the start of his five-day sentencing hearing on Monday, family members watching proceedings at Hull Crown Court gasped and were in tears as details of the "horror scene" at the parlour were described by prosecutors.

This story contains details some might find distressing.

Chris Paxton KC told the packed court bodies had been discovered "on the racks" of a cold storage area and one was found on a stretcher on the floor.

The vast majority were "uncovered and in varying states of decomposition", including one of a stillborn baby.

Bush, 48, was "entrusted by hundreds of bereaved families" but had "breached that trust on an almost industrial scale in a myriad of ways", Paxton said.

News.title: Reform UK reports Zack Polanski to police over guillotine T-shirt post
News.content:
Reform UK have reported Green Party leader Zack Polanski to the police, after he shared an Instagram post including a photo of a man wearing a top featuring the name "Nigel" alongside an image of a guillotine.

One of several images showed a man in a black t-shirt with a large guillotine below the words "We're only making plans for Nigel".

Sharing a screenshot on X, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "If I was to post anything as inciteful then I would expect to be arrested, and so should Polanski."

A Green Party spokesperson said: "Once this image was brought to [Zack's] attention he immediately unshared the post. He unequivocally does not support this type of dangerous message."

Polanski had shared the photo with his 713,000 followers in a post containing several pictures of a Green Party event on Sunday, having accepted a request to collaborate with another account.

In a post on X, the Metropolitan Police said: "We received a third-party report relating to an image shared on social media. We take reports of this nature extremely seriously, and officers are conducting enquiries into the matter."

The words "We're only making plans for Nigel" are the same as the lyrics of a 1979 song by band XTC, external.

The Green Party spokesperson said: "Zack condemns the image on the T-shirt. He was tagged in a post with 20 images and clicked accept without realising there was more to it than he had seen.

"The T-shirt is clearly in poor taste, especially at a time of heightened fears for the security of public figures, having experienced multiple threats himself.

"He and the Green Party call on everyone involved in public discourse to show kindness and not encourage more division."

The BBC understands Polanski has not been contacted by police.

News.title: Man jailed for abduction and rape of girl, 15, in Edinburgh basement
News.content:
A masked rapist who abducted a 15-year-old girl from an Edinburgh city centre bus stop has been jailed under a lifelong restriction order.

Aaron Strachan, 21, pulled a knife on the girl on the city's Princes Street in May last year, before marching her to a basement storage area and raping her.

The High Court in Edinburgh heard that he also attacked a man with a hammer days later, and had a criminal record of violence, robbery and possession of weapons.

Strachan was jailed for a minimum of five years with an order for lifelong restriction (OLR). It means a parole board must decide if he is ever safe to be released.

Judge Michael O'Grady described Strachan's crimes as the "stuff of nightmares".

Strachan admitted raping the girl and charges of serious assault against two male victims in December last year.

The judge said he expected Strachan to be in custody or under supervision for the rest of his life.

News.title: Zelensky visit sends clear message of support for Ukraine, Burnham says
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said the UK is "with Ukraine 100%" as Volodymyr Zelensky became the prime minister's first international visitor since entering No 10.

Burnham said the visit of the Ukrainian president was designed to "send a very clear message" about the UK's continued support.

"To put it simply, Volodymyr, I want you to know that we've got your back, you can count on me and you can count on us. You can count on the UK for as long as it takes," he said at a naval base in Portsmouth on Monday.

Zelensky, meanwhile, said Ukraine's relationship with the UK was "stronger than ever".

Addressing Zelensky, Burnham said: "I am personally with you 100%, Mr President, and I will honour every commitment this country has made to Ukraine in full."

Burnham added that he intended to visit Ukraine "soon" following the "very warm meeting" between the pair.

The PM also announced the sharing of the intellectual property behind the UK's new "Stone Cloak" electronic warfare system, enabling Ukraine to produce the technology at scale.

Burnham said: "It will help them to hit their targets and help save Ukrainian lives."

The Stone Cloak jammers are the size of a tablet computer and are designed to block the detection of any drones they are fitted to.

The Ministry of Defence has already given thousands of the devices to Ukrainian forces to bolster their drone operations.

Downing Street said that following its deployment in Ukraine, the technology will be built into the UK's next generation of long-range weapons.

It said this would include Project Brakestop, a government programme to develop low-cost cruise missiles - self-propelled guided weapons that fly like normal aircraft for much of their flight.

During Monday's visit, the two leaders also met more than 200 Ukrainian military personnel who have spent the last three weeks taking part in a maritime exercise in the UK.

Exercise Sea Breeze is aimed at strengthening warfighting capabilities and counter-mine measures in the Black Sea.

Burnham also said the UK would support Ukraine to get a "full and unconditional ceasefire".

"We will keep up the pressure, pushing for a ceasefire and a resumption of negotiations which must have Ukraine at the table and include a strong voice for Europe too."

News.title: TV presenter and comedian Bill Oddie dies at 85
News.content:
TV presenter and comedian Bill Oddie has died at the age of 85, his agent has said.

Oddie became a household name in the 1970s as part of zany TV comedy trio The Goodies, before concentrating on his love of wildlife, as one of the original hosts of BBC TV's Springwatch and other shows about birdwatching.

In a statement, David Foster said: "It is with deep sadness that I announce the passing of Bill Oddie, the country's best-loved birder.

"Bill was a multi-talented celebrity â wildlife presenter, broadcaster, comedian, writer, songwriter, musician and conservationist. Yet it was never fame that he valued. Instead he encouraged us to respect and protect the environment."

News.title: UK's iconic Jodrell Bank telescope faces axe in science cuts
News.content:
The Jodrell Bank Observatory, which has housed the UK's largest telescope for nearly 70 years, has lost its funding and could now close, the BBC understands.

The observatory and its network of telescopes have been pivotal to the country's study of distant galaxies and training future astronomers. Scientists have described the decision as "heartbreaking" and "scientifically misguided".

All scientific observations at Jodrell are expected to cease on the 1 April 2028 unless alternative funding can be found.

The funding body, the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) agency, said it had to focus investment on projects that deliver "the greatest long-term impact".

Prof Brian Cox, professor of particle physics at the University of Manchester - which hosts Jodrell Bank Observatory - described the cuts as "hasty and ill-considered".

"The damage to the UK's science base has already been substantial. I am astonished that UKRI are still ploughing ahead and not working with the Burnham government to find a solution," he said.

In response, Jonathan Reynolds, who is the new Secretary of State in the expanded business department that now has responsibility for science, told BBC News that the UK's world class research was "absolutely central to creating a better future for the UK".

"I am committed to working with UKRI to ensure the UK remains able not only to sustain its world-leading research capabilities, but also to invest in the next generation of scientific facilities and infrastructure that will underpin discovery, innovation and growth in the years ahead."

The Jodrell Bank site was first established in 1945 and pioneered radio astronomy and the study of galaxies beyond our own.

It was also pivotal during the Cold War, when it was used to monitor Soviet missiles during the height of nuclear tensions between the USSR and Nato powers.

Its contribution to global scientific efforts earned it Unesco World Heritage status in 2019.

But the UKRI, which has an annual budget of just under Â£10bn, says it has had to cut the observatory's annual Â£2.8m budget because planned research costs for physics and the running of its labs had escalated.

The announcement is part of broader cuts to astronomy, nuclear and particle physics research over the next four years which will also impact on other projects.

The UK will no longer participate in research at the James Clark Maxwell Telescope in Hawaii, which scientists are using to image supermassive black holes at the centre of galaxies.

UKRI has also cut funding for the UK's involvement in two instruments on the Extremely Large Telescope which is being built in Chile to search for signs of life on other Earth-like worlds.

And a number of upgrades to improve experiments at the Large Hadron Collider will not be paid for by the agency.

News.title: Teen denies endangering lives of 165 people on migrant boat crossing
News.content:
A teenager accused of endangering the lives of 165 migrants by allegedly piloting a record-breaking dinghy crossing of the English Channel is to stand trial.

Chan Mathok Atak, 19, originally of Sudan, appeared at Margate Magistrates Court earlier, where he denied endangering lives at sea during the attempt which set off from France last Thursday.

He appeared with the aid of an Arabic interpreter and when asked how he wished to plea, denied having piloted the dinghy.

Atak was then remanded into custody and will next appear at Canterbury Crown Court on 24 August.

Prosecutor Lucie Fish told the court that, on Thursday, a rigid hulled inflatable boat departed the French coast headed towards Dover carrying the migrants.

The vessel was intercepted by Border Force and Atak is alleged to be one of two people controlling its speed and travel.

The boat was poor quality, overcrowded and "appeared to be deflating upon interception", the prosecutor added.

Pictures of Border Security Command towing the dinghy into Dover showed to be about the same size as a standard bus, at 13m (42ft) long.

During the hearing, the court heard that the French authorities had recovered the body of a man who had suffered head injuries - but there was no indication in court whether his death was related to the record-breaking dinghy.

A spokesman for the National Crime Agency told BBC News: "We are aware of an incident on Thursday 23 July in which an individual died in French waters. French partners are leading the investigation into the circumstances".

Endangerment at sea is a new offence that was created by the government under Sir Keir Starmer to target those alleged to have steered small boats over the English Channel.

In June, two men were the first to be jailed for the crime, each receiving sentences of more than two years.

The previous record arrival in a single vessel was 128 people.

Home Office figures show that while the overall number of arrivals this year is down by about 45% on 2025, the number of migrants per boat has gone up.

News.title: 'Antisemitism felt relentless' - Jewish students on life at UK universities
News.content:
Like many campuses across the UK, Cardiff University has seen pro-Palestine protests in recent years and Oliver said he believed some behaviour he witnessed crossed the line from criticism of Israel into antisemitism.

Holding Jewish people responsible for the actions of the Israeli government is a form of antisemitism, according to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance.

"That first year was absolutely terrifying," he said.

"You go home and think, 'do I carry on? Do I try to go to the next day?'"

Oliver said he stopped speaking Hebrew outside his home, and hid his Star of David pendant when on campus.

Over the following three years, Oliver said the antisemitic abuse he experienced at university became "relentless".

"I've been in clubs [or] just wandering around the uni and you hear these conversations and you see pamphlets being handed around where it's literally saying that your belief and your history is fake," he said.

"I've been at house parties where, when someone's found out I'm Jewish they started calling me Netanyahu behind my back.

"Like you found out my religion and you've decided I'm a bad person."

Oliver said when he had reported antisemitic incidents that had happened to him and others, he had felt they had been often "swept under the rug" by the university.

Although he said some positive action had been taken, he feels more needs to be done.

Cardiff University said it was sorry that "any student felt unsafe" on campus and that it adopts a "zero-tolerance approach to harassment and discrimination of all kinds".

It said there was no place for antisemitism or hatred at the university and there were "robust procedures" in place for investigating allegations of antisemitism. Where it is found, the university said appropriate action would be taken.

It said it had reached out to the university's Jewish Society and reminded students to report incidents to them.

News.title: Very strong tide led to West Mersea drownings, relative says
News.content:
A mother and daughter who drowned off the Essex coast were swept out to sea by a "very strong" tide, a relative has said.

Shahin Ahmed said six members of his family were paddling at West Mersea beach when they were knocked off their feet on Wednesday afternoon.

Shelina Rahman, 41, and 15-year-old Sameeha, died in the tragedy, while Ahmed's seven-year-old son Musa was airlifted to hospital in a critical condition.

Ahmed said his son, who is from east London, remained on a life support machine at a hospital in London.

Three others were also taken to another hospital by ambulance after the incident. Ahmed said 12 of them were visiting West Mersea that day.

"This was 20 minutes before we were going to go home. The whole day, alhamdulillah (praise be to God), was really nice," Ahmed told Bangladeshi newspaper Surma News.

News.title: Ex political advisor admits fraud over expense claims
News.content:
A former advisor to a Labour MP has admitted claiming fraudulent expenses on the Parliamentary travel booking system.

Matthew Torbitt worked for Bury South MP Christian Wakeford when, between August 2022 and September 2024, he claimed rail tickets that were "not for Parliamentary purposes", Thames Magistrates' Court heard.

He also admitted making a false claim for travel and accommodation expenses on 2 October 2024.

Torbitt, 35, has most recently worked as a political commentator and regularly appears on programmes including GB News, LBC, Sky News, BBC Newsnight, and Times Radio.

Prosecutor Maisha Mannan told the court the claims totalled more than Â£6,000, according to an early estimate by the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), but the exact sum will be calculated at a later date.

Torbitt, who appeared in court dressed in a navy blue suit, pleaded guilty to two counts of fraud by false representation.

District Judge Navneet Sher sent the case to Snaresbrook Crown Court for sentence at a later date, which has yet to be fixed.

"It's unlikely to be before four weeks, in any event," she told the defendant.

Torbitt worked in various advisory roles for Labour frontbenchers between 2018 and 2024.

An investigation was launched after police received a report that a member of staff working for an MP had allegedly made unauthorised purchases through a travel booking system, the Metropolitan Police previously said.

He was charged by postal requisition on 9 June.

Torbitt is engaged to women's rights activist and 2021 Love Island contestant Sharon Gaffka.

The couple welcomed a baby boy earlier this month, according to Torbitt's Instagram page.

News.title: Fit schools, hospitals and new homes with air con, say Lib Dems
News.content:
In a report published earlier this year,, external the UK's independent adviser on tackling climate change, the Climate Change Committee (CCC), estimated that 92% of existing homes would be at risk of overheating by 2050.

Speaking to Matt Chorley on BBC Radio 5 Live, Farron said: "We want to make sure that we're not being hysterical but we're recognising that we have more extreme temperatures, more extreme weather.

"I want the homes that people live in in the future to be ready for that, that we be climate-ready and prepared."

The party said the cost of its policy to developers would be small compared to the overall cost of building a home, and that cooler homes would be more attractive to buyers in the future.

Farron said forms of air cooling systems should be installed without adding "to the climate crisis", pointing to the potential of air source heat pumps.

There have been concerns that while decreasing temperatures indoors, air conditioning units can increase outdoor temperatures.

Michael Whittall, sustainability manager at property developer Fairview New Homes, told news agency PA: "Air conditioning systems work by removing heat from inside buildings and releasing it outdoors.

"When this happens at scale, particularly in dense urban areas, it can contribute to the urban heat island effect â adding to higher outdoor temperatures and increasing heat stress in cities."

He said the focus should be on "passive cooling" such as better designs, shading and ventilation.

Amanda Williams, head of environmental sustainability at the Chartered Institute of Building (CIOB), said air conditioning or reversible heat pumps would "undoubtedly have a crucial role in some circumstances".

However, she added that making it the default option "risks locking in higher energy consumption" and that the priority should be designing homes that "remain comfortable for as much of the year as possible".

A spokesperson for the Home Builders Federation said: "New build homes are required to be exceptionally well insulated which helps keep them both warmer in winter and cooler in summer.

"This makes living in a new build more comfortable and significantly cheaper to run than older, less well-insulated homes."

The Liberal Democrats have also argued that the government should fund the cost of fitting essential buildings such as schools and hospitals with air conditioning.

The party said the costs of inaction dwarfed the costs of acting immediately, pointing to the CCC's report, external which said climate impacts could cost Â£60bn - Â£260bn a year compared to the Â£7bn - Â£22bn it would cost to protect people from the impacts.

The Lib Dems said the cost of fitting hospitals with air conditioning would come from its Â£10bn investment plan for the NHS.

News.title: 'Cruel' carer jailed for abuse yelled 'I hope you die' at 81-year-old victim
News.content:
A "heartless and cruel" carer who was caught on camera abusing an 81-year-old woman with dementia has been jailed.

In footage shared online, carer Louise Harris could be seen screaming at Elizabeth Anne Shipton in her home in Pontardawe, Neath Port Talbot, and drunkenly shouting: "I hope you die in your sleep you... horrible cow."

As Elizabeth lay in bed, Harris knelt down and put her arm on her chest, demanding to know where her money was.

Elizabeth complained the arm was hurting her, but the carer yelled: "I don't care, where's your money?"

Harris, 42, was given a three-month sentence at Swansea Crown Court - but the victim's family believes it should have been a significantly longer sentence.

Elizabethâs daughter, Tracy Faram Shipton, said her mother was "horrifically traumatised" and had filed an appeal, arguing the sentence handed to Harris last week was unduly lenient.

She had known Harris, a former neighbour, for many years and had trusted her with her mum's care.

"She'd been a carer since she was 18. I checked everything with her - she was trained on dementia, manual handling, incontinence. I'll never get my head around how she could do this," she said.

Tracy said Harris had known her mother had been in a fragile state, having recently been in Morriston hospital for seven weeks with sepsis. She was also grieving the death of her husband, who she had been with since the age of 16.

"My mother had come out of hospital in December, my dad's funeral was in January, and then this happened in February. Louise knew everything my mother was going through," she said.

Tracy said Harris was on her first trial shift, after the family had advertised on Facebook for someone to help while they had waited for a care package to be put in place by social services.

Tracy said Harris had been meant to stay for four hours in total.

"I was there for the first hour and Louise seemed amazing. Almost as soon as I left she turned," she said.

She said that, after she had left, Harris "got drunk and ripped up my mother's knitting".

"I'd explained to her that knitting was the only thing helping my mother through the grief, it was giving her something to live for... It was just cruel."

Harris found a bottle of vodka in the fridge and downed it. The court heard she was a recovering alcoholic who had "succumbed to temptation".

Harris's rage appeared to be sparked by Elizabeth accidentally pressing her emergency alarm, which triggered a phone call to a crisis response helpline.

Tracy said this had happened often and the helpline operator quickly ended the call after Harris said everything had been fine.

The court heard how, at one point, Harris went into the kitchen and waved a large kitchen knife around while trashing the property.

Tracy said she had been horrified when she had accessed the security system's camera to check how things were going, and had witnessed Harris abusing her mum.

"The police had to break the door down," she said.

Abul Hussain, prosecuting, said the victim had lain helpless in her bed thinking she was going to die.

Harris had been "slumped on the floor" when police had entered the property, he said.

Harris pleaded guilty to being a care worker who ill-treated the victim and to criminal damage.

She had originally been charged with attempted robbery because of her demands about Elizabethâs money, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) dropped that charge.

Tracy said it "beggars belief that they couldn't see any physical assault there".

Andrew Evans, representing Harris, said his client was genuinely remorseful for her "wholly unacceptable behaviour", which he said was the result of her finding the vodka in the fridge.

Judge Rees imposed a three-month jail term, of which 40% will be served in custody.

Tracy added: "The judge's hands were tied by the sentencing guidelines. You could see he was raging.

"For her to be serving just over a month is unbelievable... We've been living this day in, day out, with my mother getting worse."

She said her mum "can't be left on her own at all now".

"She keeps thinking Louise is going to come back, and she has such vivid flashbacks that she's been put on sedatives.

"The effect is my mum will not wear the lifeline device because she thinks if she presses it the same thing will happen. We've had to fit a new front door with glass in the middle so she can see if someone is on the other side."

She said she wanted all homes where carers attended to be fitted with cameras, "because what if we didn't have this camera?"

Judge Rees said elderly people were entitled to be treated with "respect, dignity and humanity" but the defendant had been "heartless and cruel", showing a "callous disregard" for her welfare.

News.title: Amber heat health alerts for parts of UK ahead of next heatwave
News.content:
Amber heat health alerts have been issued for much of eastern England for later this week as temperatures rise again.

The East Midlands, East of England, London, and the South East are all under the amber alerts from 9am on Wednesday until 9am Thursday.

With the temperature forecast to peak in the mid-30s Celsius on Wednesday, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), which issues the alerts, warns that significant impacts are likely across health and social care services due to the high temperatures.

Yorkshire and the Humber, the West Midlands, and the South West are all under less severe yellow alerts for the same period.

This latest heatwave comes after some of the driest regions of the UK missed their chance of rain over the weekend.

Parts of the northern and western UK saw some rainfall on Saturday and Sunday, with further showers and unsettled conditions expected over the next few days.

But southern parts of the country - where the least amount of rain has fallen - are set to see temperatures climb once again, with more dry and sunny weather in the forecast.

It comes as parts of Wales have officially entered drought status, while parts of southern, central and eastern England remain in "prolonged dry weather", the final stage before drought is declared.

The coming days will only exacerbate dry conditions as another heatwave is expected to be declared, with temperatures peaking around 34-35C (93-95F) in south-east England or the East of England.

News.title: NHS 'will collapse' without social care reform, PM tells BBC
News.content:
Andy Burnham has told the BBC "the NHS will collapse" if social care is not reformed but said he could not put a timeline on changes.

In his first major interview since becoming prime minister, Burnham said he would not want to leave office without bringing in "substantial change" to the social care system.

The prime minister also suggested making it harder to claim benefits, saying the country had to get serious about getting the welfare bill down.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has meanwhile written to the prime minister, saying he should rule out tax rises or increased borrowing to fund social care reform.

Burnham told the BBC that if the government did not reform social care, the NHS would "collapse under the weight of trying to care for people who've really not needed to end up in the NHS system".

But pressed on whether he would create a new system before the next election, he said he "couldn't put a timeline on it right here, right now", though he would put "whatever political capital I have into fixing broken social care".

Burnham first proposed a universal system of social care in England in 2009 when he was health secretary under Gordon Brown and pursued the idea of a compulsory levy to fund it.

That Labour government also floated the idea of allowing people to defer the payment until after they died, which led to the Tories branding it a "death tax".

Burnham is due to make a speech on adult social care on Wednesday.

The BBC understands the PM will stop short of unveiling plans for a new system in this speech, instead announcing he is speeding up the Casey Commission, an independent review that has been considering possible solutions for social care.

Baroness Louise Casey is not expected to give her final recommendations until 2028, but Burnham wants to bring her schedule forward.

Adult social care provides state support to help people live more independently, including assistance at home.

Unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use. In England and Northern Ireland, people with savings worth more than Â£23,250 are not entitled to help with care costs from their council.

In Wales and Scotland, different rules apply in terms of eligibility.

Sarah Woolnough, chief executive of healthcare think tank the King's Fund, said the current "punitive system" meant that "quite a lot of people go without care that they need", with one in seven paying in excess of Â£100,000 for social care.

While Burnham has not yet outlined any plans, Woolnough told the BBC Radio 4's Today programme that reforms could range from making social care free at the point of need to placing a cap on the amount people spend.

"The PM has for a long time mooted the idea of a social care system similar to NHS," she said.

"It would be expensive but on the scale of what we spend on other public services - around Â£200bn on the NHS - we are talking for some of these options low billions per year."

Adult social care has proved a complex issue to tackle for successive governments.

Two years ago Sir Keir Starmer was criticised when Labour scrapped plans for an Â£86,000 cap on the amount people in England would spend on social care in their lifetime.

Badenoch wrote in her letter to Burnham that "any solution to the issues around social care must also be fair to those who have made provisions and saved up over the course of their lives".

Layla Moran, the Liberal Democrat MP who chairs the Health and Social Committee, told the Today programme: "We do need to discuss where the money is going to come from but also we need to all be putting our political capital into this."

Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said he was ready to do "whatever I can to find a real and lasting consensus on social care".

"Family carers must be at the heart of any new system, everyone must get the care they need and no one should lose their home as a result," he said.

Reform Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said social care needed fixing but warned the party would fight any proposal for a "universal death tax".

He said: "It's not fair to raid people's life savings and drags hundreds of thousands more families into paying tax when their loved ones pass away."

News.title: Teens in court accused of murder after stabbing
News.content:
Three teenage boys have appeared in court charged with murder after a fatal stabbing in Luton.

Bedfordshire Police were called to reports of violent disorder at Kingsway Recreation Ground at about 18:30 BST on Friday, where a 17-year-old boy was found with stab wounds. He later died in hospital.

A 16-year-old and two 17-year-olds, who cannot be named because of their age, appeared at Luton Magistrates' Court charged with murder, violent disorder and possession of a bladed article.

They were remanded in custody pending a further court appearance.

Another 17-year-old boy arrested over the weekend has been released on bail pending further inquiries, while a further 17-year-old who was arrested on Friday, and who was being treated in hospital for serious injuries, remains in police custody.

Det Ch Insp Nick Gardener said: "We understand this was a shocking incident for the local community and we would like to reassure them that we have had detectives working tirelessly on this case throughout the weekend.

"High visibility patrols and an increased police presence in the area will continue."

News.title: Idaho murder victim’s family blast Bryan Kohberger’s bid to rescind guilty plea: ‘A mosquito you can’t seem to swat’
News.content:

The family of one of Bryan Kohberger’s victims has blasted a bid from the convicted killer to rescind his guilty plea and go to trial.

“The mosquito you just can’t seem to swat. That is what Kohberger and his following have become to this family,” relatives of Kaylee Goncalves said in a statement on Facebook Monday afternoon following Kohberger’s claim that he had been “misled” into pleading guilty.

Goncalves was just 21 years old when she and three of her college friends were stabbed to death in their off-campus house in Moscow, Idaho, in November 2022.

“He never cried wolf or claimed he was uninformed, pressured, or that there were issues with the discovery that he and his counsel had for 2 years that he thought should have been challenged,” the Goncalves family said of Kohberger. “He admitted to guilt and asked whether he actually was guilty he said ‘yes.’”

Officials had built a case against Kohberger using DNA evidence from a knife sheath found at the bloody scene and surveillance footage of a car that matched Kohberger’s in the area at the time of the murders, along with other evidence.

open image in gallery The family of one of Bryan Kohberger’s victims has blasted a bid from the convicted killer to rescind his guilty plea and go to trial ( Instagram )

Facing the death penalty if convicted of the quadruple homicide, Kohberger, now 31, confessed to the murder of Goncalves, her roommates Madison Mogen, 21, and Xana Kernodle, 20, and Kernodle’s boyfriend Ethan Chapin, 20, in July 2025 just weeks before he was supposed to stand trial.

The Goncalves’ statement came after Kohberger, a former PhD student of criminology at Washington State University, claimed “justice was not served.”

“Unanswered questions seem to multiply with each piece of discovery unsealed, and the public demands the truth,” Kohberger said in a statement to The New York Times published Monday.

“My actual innocence is my truth, and the plea, hinged on by false promises and blatant disinformation, MUST be withdrawn,” he said.

open image in gallery Kaylee Goncalves’ family has remained outspoken ever since the 21-year-old was brutally stabbed to death along with her three college friends in 2022 ( Moscow Police Department )

Kohberger filed a “petition for post conviction relief” in the Ada County District Court in Idaho Monday, NBC News reported.

The Goncalves family said should Kohberger succeed in getting another day in court, it would be a “nice break from his solitary confinement” for the killer.

“The real issue is that if as much energy was put into honoring the victims in this case as trying to set a guilty man free there would be statutes of the victims on every corner with parks and days honoring their ultimate sacrifice ‘their lives’ at the hands of narcissist,” the family wrote. “Regardless of how this turns out, our family is 100% ready. An actual trial this time? Let's go!”

The Goncalves said if there is a trial, they are “confident he will get the death penalty that he escaped by pleading guilty the first time around.”

open image in gallery Facing the death penalty if convicted of the quadruple homicide, Kohberger, now 31, confessed to the murder of Goncalves, her roommates Madison Mogen, 21, and Xana Kernodle, 20, and Kernodle’s boyfriend Ethan Chapin, 20, in July 2025 ( Getty )

While Kohberger did waive his right to an appeal or chance of parole in his plea deal, since his petition to open the case is not an appeal, it does not violate the terms of the agreement.

He is currently serving four consecutive life sentences for the murders as well as an additional ten-year sentence for burglary after he broke into the victims’ college home with the intent to kill.

The Goncalves family previously accused prosecutors of having “failed” them with Khoberger’s plea deal, saying they were “beyond furious at the State of Idaho” in a June 2025 Facebook post.

They had hoped a trial would reveal the killer’s motive, which is still unknown.

Bradley Walsh has announced he will not be hosting the popular gameshow Blankety Blank this year.

The presenter and actor attributed his departure to scheduling conflicts, saying: "I just don’t have the time.”

The beloved programme, which challenges contestants to match fill-in-the-blank answers, saw its latest revival in 2020 with Walsh at the helm.

Blankety Blank originally graced BBC screens from 1979 to 1990 and has since undergone numerous reboots.

Speaking to Radio Times, the 66-year-old broadcaster expressed his fondness for the show, admitting it is "one of my favourite shows," but confirmed he cannot return for its fourth series, set to begin filming later this year.

Walsh said: “The thing is we’re just doing Gladiators. I get a week off and then I go to rehearsals for the live Prat Pack show.

“I take The Prat Pack back on the road for a month, and then I would normally go straight into Blankety Blank.

“But at the moment, what I’m going to do is I’ve got other stuff which I can’t announce (yet).

Bradley Walsh left the door open for him to return to the show next year ( PA Archive )

“We’re working on a couple of dramas and scripting, and I actually physically do not have the time.”

“I would normally go to studio October, but I’m all taken up in October and November, so I just haven’t time to do it. Maybe next year,” he added.

The broadcaster and actor currently hosts programmes including The Chase, its international spin-off The Chase Around The World, and Gladiators, presenting the latter with his son Barney Walsh.

He also has an upcoming tour with comedy group The Prat Pack – alongside fellow stars Brian Conley, Shane Richie, and Joe Pasquale.

Walsh told the weekly magazine: “(It) is sad because I’ve loved Blankety Blank. It’s been one of my favourite shows, and it’s been brilliant.”

“It really makes me laugh. It’s the most fun you can have in the studio, and I just cannot at the moment work on it,” he added.

Walsh, who rose to fame as a stand-up comedian, and has also worked as an actor – featuring in shows such as Coronation Street, Doctor Who and Law & Order: UK.

He has presented many gameshows across his decades-long career such as Wheel Of Fortune, and more recently Odd One In, Cash Trapped, and Keep It In The Family.

Blankety Blank first aired in 1979 with Terry Wogan as the original host, and was later taken over by comedian and actor Les Dawson from 1984 until 1990.

The show was first rebooted in 1997 with the late Paul O’Grady at the helm as his drag alter ego, Lily Savage, and ran until 2002.

International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva praised Argentine President Javier Milei’s austerity policies and reform agenda Monday, saying they have restored market confidence in a country long regarded as a serial defaulter on its sovereign debt.

Georgieva, the first IMF head to visit Buenos Aires in eight years, expressed confidence that Argentina could meet its debt obligations. As the fund’s largest debtor with about $58 billion in outstanding IMF loans, Argentina faces a key repayment period beginning next year, when Milei is expected to seek reelection.

“Argentina is in a much stronger position, and this is the result of the government’s hard work and the perseverance and sacrifice of the Argentine people,” Georgieva said at a news conference alongside Economy Minister Luis Caputo.

Georgieva recalled that Argentina’s debt was among the first issues discussed when she took over as IMF managing director in 2019.

“We were debating whether the country would be able to keep up with servicing its debt obligations to everyone. That is not the question we should be asking today,” she said.

Georgieva’s visit comes as Argentina’s economic outlook has improved, with bond prices rising, central bank reserves increasing and inflation falling. Annual inflation has slowed to 33%, down sharply from 210% when Milei took office in late 2023. Last week, Moody’s upgraded Argentina’s sovereign credit rating, months after similar upgrades by S&P and Fitch.

“What we have today is a much healthier picture,” Georgieva said. “Market confidence has returned.”

Georgieva is scheduled to visit Vaca Muerta on Tuesday, one of the world’s largest reserves of unconventional oil and natural gas. Its development is expected to become one of Argentina’s main sources of foreign-currency earnings in the coming years.

Georgieva also said she sees no need for additional IMF disbursements before the 2027 presidential election.

“We may be on a good track for Argentina to join the club of emerging markets that have borrowed from the Fund, reformed their economies and borrowed no more,” Georgieva said.

Investors are closely watching Argentina’s ability to meet its upcoming debt payments. The country will begin repaying principal on its IMF loans in September, adding to its interest payments, while its broader foreign-currency debt obligations are set to rise sharply in 2027.

Caputo has said the government expects to cover those payments with funding from multilateral lenders, proceeds from privatizations and domestic borrowing rather than by returning to international capital markets.

Despite the improving economic indicators, Milei has faced declining approval ratings as his austerity policies have coincided with weak consumer spending, stagnant wages, rising household debt and a modest increase in unemployment.

The president’s declining popularity has raised questions about his prospects for reelection in 2027 and increased investor uncertainty over whether his economic reforms would continue under a future administration.

Asked about that possibility, Georgieva acknowledged that these risks are best managed "by building strong policies during the time we have now ... policies that inspire confidence among the people of the country and the international community.”

Georgieva also said Argentina still has work to do in areas including construction, expanding credit for small businesses and mortgages, and reducing informal employment.

The family of a British woman believed to have been murdered in Florida after disappearing from her home in Hampshire have paid tribute to a “truly beautiful person” and called her “the gentlest soul”.

Sonia Exelby was reported missing from her address in Southsea, Portsmouth, on October 12 2025.

By this time, initial police inquiries established she had already left the country.

Her body was found by US investigators in Marion County, Florida, five days later.

Dwain Hall, 53, of Ocala, was subsequently arrested on charges of first-degree murder and kidnapping by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE).

He had already been detained over the alleged fraudulent use of Ms Exelby’s credit cards.

Hall is expected to face trial in November.

In a statement released by Hampshire police on behalf of the family, they said: “Sonia was a truly beautiful person, inside and out.

open image in gallery Sonia Exelby was the the youngest of six children and was ‘deeply loved by all her siblings’, her family said ( Family Handout/PA Wire )

“She had the gentlest soul – so gentle that she chose to become vegan, because she couldn’t bear the thought of any animal suffering just so she could eat. That was who she was: kind, compassionate, and full of quiet love.

“She was incredibly talented. Sonia could play the piano so effortlessly, and when she sang, she had the voice of an angel. Being around her felt special — she brought a calmness and warmth that made everything feel a little lighter.

“Sonia was one of those rare people who made you feel completely safe to be yourself. She never judged, never criticised – she simply accepted people as they were and loved them for it. That is something so many of us will carry with us forever.”

The youngest of six children, the family said she was “deeply loved by all her siblings”.

The family added: “She was softly spoken and always gave the best most intense hugs. She was the baby out of us that kept us bound together.

“We will never get over losing her, which has left an emptiness in our lives that can never be filled. The world has lost so much kindness and light, and her absence will be felt by so many people for so many years to come.

“We know that life wasn’t always easy for you, but your life was so much more than the struggles you faced. This is so important to us that the life you lived is what you are remembered for.

“You were deeply loved, and you will always be deeply loved. We miss you more than words can ever say. We love you so much, always, and forever.”

The Hampshire force said: “We received a report on Sunday October 12 that Sonia was missing from her home in Southsea.

“Initial inquiries established that she had travelled outside of the UK prior to the report being received.”

It said the constabulary was continuing to support the FDLE investigation, while specially trained officers were providing assistance to Ms Exelby’s family in the UK.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune and other senior Republicans are pushing back after Donald Trump demanded Monday that they cancel the chamber’s month-long August recess and stay in town to pass voter ID legislation.

Trump, in a Truth Social post early in the day, reiterated his call for senators to stay in town for the month of August to pass the SAVE America Act, a piece of voter ID legislation he wants to see implemented before the midterms elections. He demanded, in his post, that Thune and the GOP caucus terminate the legislative filibuster to accomplish this goal, something Thune insists he will not do and does not have the votes to accomplish.

The GOP Senate leader and other Republicans made frustrated comments to reporters on Monday claiming that Trump oversold the Senate’s ability to pass voter ID legislation to Republican voters, and refusing to stay in town to take up legislation that could not pass a 60-vote filibuster threshold.

Thune was clearly on the edge of his patience with the White House as he spoke to reporters on Monday.

“We could stay here ‘til Christmas,” said the Republican leader. “Democrats aren't voting for this, I'm just telling you. And Republicans are not getting rid of the legislative filibuster.”

open image in gallery John Thune responded on Monday after Donald Trump called on him to keep senators in town for the month of August ( Getty )

"If I thought there was a path to getting a result, I'm all for it,” he added of cancelling the August recess. “But if we are going to be sitting here and in endless quorum calls, I don't know if that's in anybody's best interest."

This is a breaking news report. More to follow...
