With less than 100 days before high-stakes midterm elections, Donald Trump is asking the Supreme Court to let him enforce an executive order that would impose sweeping restrictions on mail-in voting.

Monday’s emergency request followed last week’s federal appeals court decision that upheld a judge’s ruling to block the president’s executive action, which threatened to disenfranchise “many eligible voters” by restricting U.S. Postal Service delivery of ballots to people who did not appear on a newly mandated list of eligible voters.

The appeals’ court majority determined that “unprecedented levels of involvement by federal officials in how states administer elections” would spark mass confusion and “threaten disenfranchisement of many eligible voters.” even a Trump appointee on the three-judge panel agreed in a separate opinion that the president’s order could impose “concrete injury” to legal voting.

Trump — who has spent years baselessly insisting that voting by mail is ripe for fraud, and that manipulated ballots were “rigged” against him in elections he lost — is simultaneously demanding the Senate pass his SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register to vote, among other restrictions.

Voting rights groups fear the president’s efforts to centralize control over election administration, which is left to the states, is an attempt to boost Republican candidates and suppress Democratic turnout ahead of November elections that could determine the balance of power in Congress — and the fate of Trump’s remaining years in office.

open image in gallery ( Getty )

In March, Trump issued an executive order that would require states to compile lists of eligible voters based on information from his own administration. Those lists would be compiled by the Department of Homeland Security and the Social Security Administration.

The Postal Service would then be blocked from mailing ballots to anyone who did not appear on those lists.

“The cheating on mail-in voting is legendary,” Trump said during a signing ceremony at the White House. “I think this will help a lot with elections.”

A coalition of 23 states and Washington, D.C. then sued to block the order, fearing that countless eligible voters could be left off the lists. Last month, U.S. District Judge India Talwani determined that “the Constitution reserves the power to determine voter eligibility to the States alone,” and even if the federal government was to be involved, it’s unlikely to be able to keep track of name changes and new addresses that could end up preventing otherwise eligible voters from receiving ballots under Trump’s rules.

“It is clear that the federal agencies charged with compiling Confirmed Citizen Lists lack the ability to create complete and accurate lists of the U.S. citizens residing in every State,” she wrote.

Data compiled by the federal government was set to be handed off to state election officials before citizens could check to see if their information is accurate — which could force eligible voters from state voter rolls without recourse.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

Trump’s latest legal fight at the nation’s hight court follows a series of White House-directed actions targeting the nation’s elections and the people who run them.

The administration — fueled by the president’s obsession with his loss in the 2020 election and baseless allegations that the results were rigged against him — has launched a sweeping attack on the nation’s election infrastructure since returning to office last year while Republican allies raced to carve up election maps before midterm elections this fall.

A false claim that millions of noncitizens are voting in federal elections is also fueling the push for Trump’s SAVE America Act, and the president is calling on Republican senators to blow up the Senate filibuster and stuff the legislation into other bills to get it passed.

The Department of Justice has also threatened criminal charges against election officials in every state if they knowingly permit noncitizens to vote or remain on voter rolls.

Election officials and voting rights groups fear the administration’s threats could be used to intimidate election workers and chill voter participation.

News.title: Human first, athlete second: Ramsay-Peaty finds peace despite second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

News.title: Amazon has ended support for pre-2013 Kindles. What to do if you’re affected (and what to avoid)
News.content:
It seems like a lot of devices, but Amazon told Engadget that the move will affect around three per cent of current users. In theory, if you’re using a device that’s affected, then Amazon should already have notified you via email. If in doubt, however, the company has a support page with pictures and specifications of every Kindle ever released. If you’re still unsure, entering the model number into Google should reveal the exact version you’re using. This can typically be found on the back of devices.

For Kindle Fire tablets, the process is simpler. Open the Settings menu and select “Device Options”. You’ll find the model you’re using either under “Device Model” or “About Fire Tablet”.

Why did this happen?

Nobody expects electronic devices to be supported forever, but it’s disappointing that the Kindle’s most enthusiastic early adopters got cut off. Given the basic functionality of e-book reader technology, there doesn’t appear to be a technical reason behind the decision, making it appear like an anti-consumer move to push older customers towards the purchase of newer devices where existing Kindles would become an e-waste casualty.

When asked why these devices were losing support, we received a response defending the (admittedly impressive) longevity.

“These models have been supported for at least 14 years – some as long as 18 years – but technology has come a long way in that time, and these devices will no longer be supported moving forward,” an Amazon spokesperson said. “We are notifying those still actively using them and offering promotions to help with the transition to newer devices.”

At the initial time of writing, the promotions mentioned appeared to be 20 per cent off “select new Kindle devices” alongside a £15 eBook credit. While the latter was welcome, the highlighted discount is somewhat disappointing for a number of reasons. Firstly, according to the promotion’s terms and conditions, the “select” caveat excludes the most expensive model, the Kindle Scribe. It doesn’t apply to Fire devices for those tablet owners looking to replace like-for-like, either.

More importantly, the prices aren’t all that impressive considering happy owners of older Kindles weren’t budgeting for this purchase. Amazon frequently discounts its own-brand devices like Echo smart speakers and Fire tablets, and 20 per cent isn’t that unusual. Last year’s Black Friday sale saw discounts of over 30 per cent on the basic Kindle and Kindle Colorsoft, and the price-tracking site CamelCamelCamel shows that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition has been as low as £183 in the past – a 32 per cent discount on its current price of £269.

There was added time pressure, too. Amazon said the discount and credit offer was only valid until June 20, one month after support for the older Kindles ended.

Additionally, owners of the earliest UK Kindle will see that prices have gone up over the past decade. The £109 they paid in 2010 is some way off the £159.99 Kindle Paperwhite, even with a 20 per cent discount, let alone the £219.99 Kindle Colorsoft. That said, at £94.99, the basic Kindle 12th Generation remains a bargain for no-frills readers, with a 20 per cent discount taking it down to £75.99.

Possible upgrades

If you’re affected by this news, the silver lining is that while e-book technology moves relatively slowly, things have still advanced significantly in the past 14 years. Resolutions are higher; most are backlit for bedtime reading; there’s support for audiobooks; and storage has increased. There are also optional extras like colour screens, blue-light filters to prevent eye strain and waterproofing.

As outlined in our guide to the best Kindles, our pick for most people is the 12th Generation Kindle Paperwhite, which costs £159.99 with lockscreen ads or £169.99 without. The seven inch screen with warm lighting makes for a comfortable reading experience, and it’s waterproof for bathtime or poolside reading.

At £94.99 (or £104.99 without ads), the basic 11th Generation Kindle is a great budget pick, however. It’s slightly smaller at six inches, and like the Paperwhite, can hold around 8,000 e-books with support for audiobooks through Audible. It lacks the warm light and waterproofing, however, and its battery life is around half that of the Paperwhite — albeit still a generous six weeks of normal use.

The two remaining Kindles occupy specific niches. The Kindle Colorsoft has a colour screen, making it well suited to those who enjoy graphic novels. The Kindle Scribe, meanwhile, has a bundled stylus for note taking.

Can I still use my old Kindle?

Yes, Amazon said users would be able to “continue to read books already downloaded on these devices”. If you factory reset your older Kindle, however, or you deregister it, you won’t be able to use it anymore.

News.title: Lando Norris comes in from the cold with dominant Hungarian GP victory
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

Sports.title: Lionel Scaloni pleads with Argentina fans as he is blocked from seeing DENTIST
Sports.content:
Lionel Scaloni pleads with Argentina fans as he is blocked from seeing DENTIST

Lionel Scaloni has returned home after guiding Argentina to the World Cup final, where his team surrendered their grip on the trophy and were beaten 1-0 by Spain in extra-time

View Image Lionel Scaloni was mobbed by fans

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni had to plead with fans blocking his way to the DENTIST after returning home from the World Cup. Scaloni's side suffered heartbreak in last Sunday's final when they lost 1-0 to Spain in extra-time.

‌



Argentina came into this summer's World Cup among the favourites, having won their last three tournaments under Scaloni. But Ferran Torres' late goal saw the trophy go to Spain, who dominated the final in New Jersey.

‌



But the 48-year-old still came home to a hero's welcome. Supporters have even been camping on his garden lawn in the town of Pujato, close to Rosario.

‌



Footage from a video which has gone viral shows Scaloni attempting to make his way through the adoring fans while security usher him to a car. The former West Ham defender gave high-fives to some children, while adults tried having a moment with their beloved boss.

Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

"I have a dentist appointment," he can heard telling the crowd. "I will be back soon."

‌



Scaloni has now left Pujato, with his family having to put a note on the door after fans continued to turn up. "Leo left last night!!! Thanks for all the love."

In a classy move, Scalno is said have come out of his house every afternoon to greet them. The Albiceleste manager signed autographs and posed for selfies with supporters of all ages.

Football fans on social media have been stunned by the warm reception. "It's as though they won the World Cup. Massive love," one posted on X.

‌



What do you make of Argentina's performance at the World Cup? Have your say in the comments section.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"Best manager in their history," another concluded on Reddit. A third said: "Nice guy for doing all that for the fans. It seems overwhelming though, to have so many people surrounding him all the time."

‌



One user agreed and wrote: "Bro literally can't go home without being hounded. That's gotta feel insane."

It's been an emotional eight days for Scaloni, who lifted the World Cup four years ago to earn himself immortality in his homeland. This year's final didn't go their way and Scaloni broke down in tears during his post-match press conference.

He posted a statement via Instagram on Monday, writing: "After an intense week where sadness intertwined with joy, tears with smiles, anguish with tranquillity, and nerves with calm, I can finally sit down to write a few words. Although you know I'm not big on social media, it might be the best way to get this message to you.

‌



"All I can say is I'm sorry I couldn't bring home another trophy and give you a new reason to celebrate - something that, even if only for a few days, might have made you forget life's hardships.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"But I want you to focus on what we tried to show you through this group of players - my warriors, as I called them when speaking about them to my wife. The effort, the drive, the desire, the 'I can do it' attitude, refusing to give up (even when the odds are stacked against you).

‌



"Giving your all (even when you have nothing left), weathering the cold showers of criticism (FROM PEOPLE WHO DON'T KNOW US), maintaining composure. And finding the will to stay on your feet when your legs no longer obey your brain…That is the true trophy.

"I am eternally grateful to my coaching staff, the players, the AFA staff - those who work quietly behind the scenes to ensure our comfort - and to each and every one of you for the affection you've shown us.

"P.S. Whoever has an Argentine friend has a treasure."

Sports.title: John Stones decides next club after England star holds talks with Chelsea
Sports.content:
John Stones decides next club after England star holds talks with Chelsea

John Stones is eyeing his next club after leaving Manchester City at the end of the season and, despite talks with Chelsea, has decided on his next move

View 2 Images John Stones has turned down the chance to sign for Chelsea

John Stones has decided to move abroad following his Manchester City exit despite holding talks with Chelsea over a possible switch.

‌



The England centre-half has just called time on his decade at the Etihad, which saw him win the Premier League on six occasions as well as the Champions League. The 32-year-old remains a strong performer and wasn't shy of suitors this summer.

‌



Chelsea were keen to add his quality and experience to their ranks with Xabi Alonso now in charge and multiple rounds of talks were held with the Blues. Ultimately Stones rejected the prospect of a move to Stamford Bridge to pursue his ambitions of playing elsewhere in Europe.

‌



Stones has played for Barnsley, Everton and City but is now closing in on a move to Inter Milan, according to reports. An agreement in principle has been secured with the Englishman, who has agreed on a deal until 2028.

Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing READ MORE :

Inter will go into the campaign as defending champions having won Serie A, their second Italian title in the last three years. They currently boast no English players in their ranks but a move to the San Siro would allow Stones to reignite his relationship with Manuel Akanji, whom he played with at City.

‌



Another Three Lions defender in Fikayo Tomori is playing at city rivals AC Milan, where he's been since 2021, although he is being linked with a move away.

Stones will bring the ball-playing ability that first attracted Pep Guardiola, who encouraged him to adopt more of a midfield role during his time in Manchester.

View 2 Images Inter Milan are poised to add the England defender

Article continues below

The veteran defender spoke in glowing terms about his time in Manchester, where he helped the club enjoyed their most successful period ever. He said: “It’s been a roller coaster. You can look at it like that and everything has ups and downs and good things, bad things. But to live out all my dreams and all my goals and all the things that I set out to achieve as a player and live as a player.

“Doing that has just been a dream and to be able to give that to everyone and do it in the style and fashion that we have and make everyone’s dream come true with obviously that Treble season, something that the club’s never achieved or won. It’s been so special.”

Sports.title: Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked
Sports.content:
Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked

Paolo Maldini has reportedly quit as Italy's technical director after just over two weeks in the role following the decision to block Andrea Pirlo from becoming manager

View 2 Images Paolo Maldini has quit his role with Italy

Italy's technical director Paolo Maldini has quit after only 16 days having seen Andrea Pirlo blocked for the vacant manager's role, according to reports.

‌



The Azzurri are on the lookout for a new boss after Gennaro Gattuso quit following another failure to qualify for the World Cup. As part of a huge reset Maldini, who played his entire career at AC Milan and won 126 caps for his country, was hired into a senior role.

‌



He was tasked with restoring Italy to their former glory and the all-time great defender had pushed for Pirlo’s appointment. After seeing that request turned down Sky Italy claim he has now walked away after just over two weeks in his job.

‌



Pirlo, part of the victorious 2006 World Cup side, expressed his frustration at being snubbed with a post on social media. He wrote: "After learning last night that I am no longer the candidate to lead the Italian national team, I believe it is my duty to clarify a few points.

Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

"In the last few days I have witnessed with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking over the role of head coach of the Italian national team.

Pirlo was not allowed to take on the role because of his connections to the Russian betting company Fonbet, where he is a brand ambassador. The former player has said it is “strictly commercial and sporting in nature”. Some involved in the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), as well as politicians, didn't think it was right he took up the post due to the ongoing war in Ukraine.

‌



Pirlo is ultimately the third major name to miss out on the role. Pep Guardiola said no for personal reasons and Carlo Ancelotti didn't want to leave his gig with Brazil.

View 2 Images Andrea Pirlo was overlooked for the role due to ties with Russia (Image: Gabriele Siri/IPA Sport/ipa-agency.net/REX/Shutterstock)

Gattuso resigned in April after Italy’s failure to qualify for this summer’s World Cup. They finished below Norway in qualifying and then lost to Bosnia-Herzegovina on penalties in the play-offs.

Article continues below

It further amplified Italy's decline with the Azzurri now missing out on the 2018, 2022 and 2026 editions. They became the first winner in history to fail to qualify for three tournaments on the bounce as their Euros success of five years ago continues to look like a distant memory.

Italy came into those championships off the back of a sensational unbeaten run and downed the likes of Belgium and Spain before beating England at Wembley in the final. Roberto Mancini was their manager but, despite some high profile men taking the job since, they continue to fall short.

Sports.title: Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing
Sports.content:
Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing

Jordan Henderson is a target for multiple Premier League clubs, with Brentford willing to let him go on a free transfer, and Chelsea are understood to be leading the race for his services

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson is another shock target for Chelsea (Image: Adrian Dennis/AFP via Getty Images)

Chelsea are working on a surprise move for Jordan Henderson, sitting first in the queue of Premier League clubs who are interested in signing him. Henderson, 36, has an agreement which will him to leave Brentford on a free transfer, despite having one year left on his contract.

‌



The midfielder is currently injured after breaking his arm during England's celebrations following their last-16 win against Mexico at the World Cup. Henderson stayed in North America for the rest of the tournament, remaining a key figure within the dressing room.

‌



His leadership and experience are part of why Xabi Alonso wants to bring him to Stamford Bridge. The Athletic report that Chelsea are the leading contenders for the former Liverpool captain's signature.

‌



It's added that multiple Premier League clubs also want to sign him. Chelsea's interest comes after they opened talks with Brighton to sign 35-year-old Danny Welbeck, further proof of their change of transfer policy since Alonso was appointed.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Last month, the Blues bid £8m for Granit Xhaka after the Sunderland captain signalled that he'd be willing reunite with Alonso, who he played under at Bayer Leverkusen. Sunderland flatly rejected the offer and Xhaka will stay.

‌



Henderson is seen as alternative, with Alonso wanting an experienced head in midfield, while he also gets on well with Chelsea's new £117million signing, Morgan Rogers. The England international only joined Brentford a year ago from Ajax, previously playing for Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq having left Liverpool in July 2023.

But his impact off the pitch is valued, too. After beating France 6-4 in the World Cup third-place play-off, England boss Thomas Tuchel revealed that the 35-year-old had given a powerful speech pre-match speech which motivated his team-mates.

"Jordan Henderson gave a very impressive speech today in the hotel to put this in the right frame and put everyone in the right mindset," Tuchel explained. "So he helped unbelievably today.

‌



Should Jordan Henderson join Chelsea? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson stayed with the England squad, despite breaking his arm (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

"That was very emotional and very, very impressive to put this game into perspective. I won't say what he said, but it puts into it perspective because he was part of this match eight years ago.

‌



"It was very emotional and he put into perspective what you might feel in the very moment, that you might give in to the feeling 'I don't want to be here'. He took all of that away because he said that it means the world in the end, and he would give anything if he hadn't broken his arm to be part again in this match.

"You never know when you get a World Cup match for England. He said it much, much better than me and more emotional, and it was very impressive. He set the tone and the mindset for this match."

Sports.content:
Man Utd star takes drastic action as Ruben Amorim plots transfer reunion

One Manchester United player could be set for a departure from Old Trafford and a reunion with a former boss in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Manchester United star Noussair Mazraoui has been linked with a reunion with Ruben Amorim (Image: (Photo by Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Manchester United defender Noussair Mazraoui has reportedly switched agents as speculation continues to mount regarding a potential departure from Old Trafford. Reports earlier this summer suggested new AC Milan manager and former United boss Ruben Amorim was interested in reuniting with the Morocco international.

‌



The Serie A outfit is searching for a wing-back to feature in Amorim's favoured 3-4-3 system, with Mazraoui being considered. Italian reports indicate the Serie A side would pursue a deal for the United defender, provided decision-makers at Old Trafford signal their willingness to sell.

‌



Amorim had previously heaped praise on Mazraoui during his Old Trafford tenure, saying: "He’s a top player. He understands the game. He knows how to attack, he’s very technical, he’s very good defensively and he’s very good one-on-one."

‌



There are, however, questions about what position the Moroccan World Cup star would occupy in Amorim's setup, having also featured as a centre-back under the Portuguese manager during his spell at Old Trafford. According to Fabrizio Romano, Mazraoui has joined new agency Panthera, who will handle his representation going forward, though it's unclear whether there's any direct link between that choice and a potential transfer this summer.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

There are, however, questions about what position the Moroccan World Cup star would occupy in Amorim's setup, having also featured as a centre-back under the Portuguese manager during his spell at Old Trafford. According to Fabrizio Romano, Mazraoui has joined new agency Panthera, who will handle his representation going forward, though it's unclear whether there's any direct link between that choice and a potential transfer this summer.

‌



Amorim, speaking in December 2024, added: "He’s a modern player. I think he’s the future of our team. When you think about him, you think we need more players like Nous that can control the tempo, they are really, really good and comfortable with the ball. So, Nous, I’m really happy with him."

The Moroccan defender was a regular for his country as they reached the latter stages of the World Cup, just a few months on from reaching the African Cup of Nations final. The 28-year-old defender made 20 appearances for United last season, sitting out a substantial portion of the campaign for the African Cup of Nations.

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim could raid his former club (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Mazraoui found it difficult to regain his spot in Michael Carrick's team after coming back from the winter competition, but did catch the eye of the then-interim United manager, eventually reclaiming his place in the starting XI.

"Yeah he's come back well, Nous," Carrick said last season after reintegrating Mazraoui back into the side. "It was a difficult one, obviously, on the back of the final and how it panned out.

"[He had] a few days to digest that then back in and around it. He's been fantastic in and around the group and around training.

Article continues below

"Obviously, he came on at the end of the game and played a part for us, as you'd expect. So yeah, again [we want to] just keep thickening the squad, bolstering the squad and it's great to have him back."

Sports.title: Man Utd get fresh Benjamin Sesko injury update after star missed pre-season friendlies
Sports.content:
Man Utd get fresh Benjamin Sesko injury update after star missed pre-season friendlies

Benjamin Sesko continues to edge towards full fitness after missing Manchester United's early pre-season friendlies and is on target to play in their Premier League opener

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko is on course to be fit for the start of the Premier League

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko is on course to be fit before the Premier League season starts despite missing successive pre-season friendlies.

‌



The Slovenian has been struggling with a shin injury and that meant he was absent for games against Wrexham and Rosenborg as he continues to follow a rehabilitation program. Sesko was already nursing a shin injury that he aggravated in the win over Liverpool in early May.

‌



United kept their cards close to their chest regarding the extent of the injury at the time as the striker missed the last three games of the campaign having been a regular up until then.

‌



However, The Sun reports that Sesko’s recovery is going to plan and he was never scheduled to participate in their opening two friendlies.

7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season READ MORE :

The ex-RB Leipzig man began outdoor training last week and has a chance of being involved against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm on Saturday as he bids to build on what was an impressive debut season, despite a slow start leading to some doubts over his signing.

‌



Sesko is likely to start against PSG in Gothenburg on August 8 before the entire United squad fly from Sweden to Dublin for a six-day training camp. The Red Devils play Leeds at Croke Park on August 12.

United begin their Premier League season against Hull City on August 22 as Michael Carrick prepares for his first full season in charge following a stellar spell in the dugout as an interim, with his results ultimately landing him the job permanently. Sesko's goals proved crucial to their run of 12 wins in 17 games.

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko's last game was the win over Liverpool, where he aggravated an injury (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The Slovenian became a super sub in Carrick's early days, coming off the bench to score the winner against Fulham and then Everton a few weeks later. In between that he scored a stoppage-time leveller at West Ham. Sesko also scored crucial goals in wins over Crystal Palace, Brentford and Liverpool as he ended his debut campaign with 12 goals.

His injury absence has allowed Joshua Zirkzee to start in the recently friendlies, despite United’s preference to sell him. The Dutchman was signed by Erik ten Hag but has struggled to live up to expectations and is very much a squad player. Zirkzee is linked with a return to Italy, but the club need to find a buyer at the right price.

Sports.content:
Man Utd in 'advanced talks' with European giants over Joshua Zirkzee exit

Joshua Zirkzee started just one of Michael Carrick's 17 games in charge last season and the Manchester United star looks to be on his way out of Old Trafford, with Juventus keen to sign him

View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee wants to leave Manchester United (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

Manchester United are in advanced talks with Juventus, who are negotiating a deal to sign Joshua Zirkzee on loan with a £30million option to buy. Zirkzee, 25, finds himself out of favour at Old Trafford, with Michael Carrick's appointment last season failing to change his fortunes.

‌



Having started just one of the 17 games Carrick was in charge for, the striker missed out on making the Netherlands' 26-man squad for the World Cup. Zirkzee only scored two goals last season, his most recent coming in December against soon-to-be relegated Wolves.

‌



After Juventus' move for Paris Saint-Germain forward Randal Kolo Muani collapsed, their focus is on Zirkzee. The Sun report that Juve are leading the race to sign him, with fellow Italian giants Roma also interested.

‌



It's understood that Zirkzee is keen on a return to Serie A. The former Bayern Munich star scored 14 goals and provided eight assists in 58 games for Bologna which convinced United to shell out £36.5m to sign him in 2024.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits READ MORE :

Zirkzee was impressive in United's second pre-season friendly on Friday. He scored a superb solo goal and registered an assist as they thrashed Rosenborg 5-0 in Norway.

‌



His departure would, though, leave United short of options at striker. Benjamin Sesko is the only senior centre forward in Carrick's squad, although they've been tipped to sign an experienced backup.

Marcus Rashford can also play in the role, having returned from a season-long loan at Barcelona. Midfield and goalkeeper are the areas in which United have done business so far, making three signings for a total of £85m.

Should Manchester United sell Joshua Zirkzee? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee scored and assisted as Manchester United beat Rosenborg 5-0 (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Dutch legend Ruud Gullit previously urged Zirkzee to leave Old Trafford and return to Serie A. "Joshua Zirkzee made a mistake moving to Manchester United - he should have stayed in Italy," Gullit told Gambling Insider.

"When he left Bologna, he should have gone to Juventus or AC Milan and stayed in Serie A. He arrived at United when there was a lot of bad energy around the club. It was the wrong time for him.

Article continues below

"There have been rumours that he could now leave United and go to Roma in the summer. I hope he makes that move, or at least join another club in Italy, because it is a much more suitable league for him."

Sports.title: Brundle's verdict on 'relentless' Norris, Piastri-Sainz incident and Malaysia return
Sports.content:
The Hungarian Grand Prix was an entertaining way to finish the first part of the 2026 F1 season before the summer break. The top four or five runners were often all visible in the same camera shot, and that included drivers from all four front running teams.

Lando Norris was on brilliant form and took both pole position and the victory, but not without a serious fight in both respects. It wasn't one of those days where a driver leads every lap from pole position and takes fastest lap. Oscar Piastri seized the lead in the second corner of the race, and Charles Leclerc in his Ferrari secured fastest lap but could only muster a fourth-place finish, and that would have been fifth had Lewis Hamilton in the sister Ferrari not attracted yet another penalty, this time for speeding in the pit-lane by 0.1kph.

It turns out Lewis did release the speed limiter a fraction early in order to beat Kimi Antonelli, who was on track, to the all-important safety car line which crosses the entire track and which decides who has the right to be in front, the driver exiting the pits, or the driver on track. It was declared that Antonelli was there a fraction earlier, and so Hamilton had to yield anyway. It was a pivotal moment for the final podium place and therefore the decision that speeding in the pitlane was a potentially competitive advantage was correct, however small the margin.

Relentless Norris and unfortunate Piastri

Norris was on the radio saying that he was faster than team-mate Piastri in the lead, without specifically asking to be let through. Then he asked to pit first, but the pit wall rightly denied that as team protocol is that the leading of the two drivers has first option on stopping.

It was beginning to look like Norris' slide wide in Turn 2 and handing the lead to Piastri would cost him a victory. McLaren pitted Piastri on Lap 16 to cover off the pit stops from Hamilton and Verstappen, and Norris next lap around on Lap 17.

But it was the second round of stops on this high tyre wear circuit that made the difference. Piastri pitted on Lap 33 again to cover Hamilton on fresh tyres, and then Norris had his chance to prove he was indeed faster by running hard and pitting on Lap 39, giving him a decent tyre life offset to his team-mate Piastri.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

Through the latter stages of the race lapped drivers appeared to be slow or even reluctant to clear the way for the leaders coming through, and it turns out there was an issue with the blue light warning system. That does still leave mirrors and team radio though.

On that same Lap 39, Piastri was coming up to lap Carlos Sainz's Williams who was having his own battle with fellow countryman Fernando Alonso, and after running wide in the infamous Turn 2 which had given Piastri the lead on the opening lap, and which must have looked for all the world to Piastri that he'd seen him and was letting him through, just as Sainz swung heavily back to the racing line and clashed with the race leader.

Sainz had been informed by his Williams team but his position on the outside of a 180 degree turn meant he had no mirror sight of Piastri tight on the inside, and so his penalty was mitigated down to five seconds, which was zero comfort to a rightly angry Piastri.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri was livid after Carlos Sainz makes contact with him in Hungary

Piastri did well not to spin out but he lost crucial time and Norris would emerge from the pits into a lead he would not relinquish. In fact, he would relentlessly increase it despite a third stop under a Virtual Safety Car for fresher soft compound tyres on Lap 56 to recover, so painfully, Piastri's McLaren which had suffered transmission failure.

The young Australian hasn't been able to catch any kind of lucky break for the best part of a year now.

Verstappen fights off Ferraris

Max Verstappen spent much of the race complaining about aerodynamic degradation, poor handling, and inconsistent gear shifting with his Red Bull, but would finish in a fine second place after some impressive overtakes on Hamilton's Ferrari. Max thought Lewis was a bit tough on him in the braking zone, but he wasn't.

It was explained to me that if the Red Bull has any damage on the aero parts particularly underneath the car, on an aggressive kerb for example, this has a disproportionate affect on the overall downforce and so grip. Hence Max's aero degradation comment.

Ferrari had looked the team to beat throughout practice, and most folk in the paddock thought they were favourites even though Norris pipped them to pole. Hamilton had smartly saved a brand new set of soft tyres by clearing the first stage of qualifying on medium tyres. These would have been extremely handy from his front-row grid slot, but he attracted a three-place grid drop from a rather brutal but unintentional blocking of another driver who was on his final qualifying attempt. You'll not be surprised to read the blocked driver was Piastri.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen shocks Lewis Hamilton with a stunning overtake at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Leclerc fluffed his qualifying with a delete lap time for track limits, and had only managed to save a set of lightly used soft tyres to start the race with. You may remember that Ferrari humbled the entire pack from the start down to the first corner in the earlier races of the season, but such is the development curve in this business, even with a tyre advantage, Hamilton only made up one place on the opening lap and Leclerc, starting on the right hand and dirtier side of the grid, fell from the front row to fifth. And now they had to manage those soft tyres and following other cars, and so their race was immediately compromised.

Ferrari would try to help Hamilton with relatively early stops on Laps 13 and 30 for the speed of fresh tyres. But with Verstappen's combative prowess this paid no dividends. Ferrari pitted both drivers again under the Lap 56 Virtual Safety Car for fresher soft tyres but that only served to allow Antonelli to get ahead (as explained earlier), a position he would keep to the final podium spot.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton responds to his speeding penalty from the Hungarian Grand Prix

Mercedes curiously off the pace

Having dominated this season so far, Mercedes were curiously off the ultimate pace, and a three-place grid penalty for Antonelli for failing to sufficiently lift for yellow warning flags in qualifying when Verstappen spun in the final corner, meant that he had lined up seventh, one place behind team-mate George Russell who was also struggling for pace.

George had also collected some engine damage with a run over the kerbs in Turn 4 and would need a new power unit fitted for race day. Whether all this new kit was responsible for a truly awful start is not so far certain, but Toto Wolff seemed clear it was a car issue.

Everything on a racing car, and especially a Formula 1 car, is positioned as low as absolutely possible to lower the centre of gravity, and so helping the handling through corners, and this leaves components vulnerable.

Russell would drop all the way back to 21st and begin a long afternoon fighting back to seventh place, tantalisingly close to Isack Hadjar's Red Bull in sixth.

Antonelli would secure that podium to increase his championship lead to 50 points over Hamilton heading into the break, and 59 points over his team-mate Russell. That's very much the definition of 'damage limitation' from seventh on the grid in such a competitive field on a circuit notoriously difficult for overtaking.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell and Kimi Antonelli react to their respective seventh and third place finishes at the Hungarian Grand Prix

Liam Lawson would finish a fine eighth and Arvid Lindblad 10th for Racing Bulls to move them up into a fifth in the Constructors' Championship ahead of Alpine. What a happy and cohesive team that appears to be.

And Nico Hulkenberg scored two points for Audi in ninth. In my mind's eye, so far this season I think of Audi consistently around and inside the top ten on pace, but actually they are eighth of 11 teams in the championship, underlining that with an improvement in reliability they can be strong contenders in the relentless midfield battle in the second half.

Aston Martin made a decent jump in performance with a comprehensive aero upgrade, and apparently leapfrogging Cadillac and Williams, and threatening Haas, all at once, but they along with Honda still have a long way to go. Nonetheless it was finally encouraging for the Silverstone team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso says Aston Martin’s new upgrades have delivered the improvements they expected, making the car easier to drive, but admits there is still more potential to unlock

Championship far from over

If McLaren have made a decent upgrade step which translates well to other circuits, this was the team's 14th Hungaroring victory, and with the top four are ever closer, this championship is far from over. There are still 291 points available assuming all the remaining races take place given the Middle East conflict.

On that subject, the Bahrain GP will now be run at the very popular Sepang circuit in Malaysia. This is the same impressive lateral thinking and flexibility F1 and its partners showed during the pandemic and I applaud it.

It sounds as if there will definitely be a European replacement race in late November or early December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi can't take place. We may need to fit some headlights and wipers for that race but the teams and drivers will handle it in their stride as usual.

I wish you all a happy summer break.

MB

Sports.title: 'Pressure is on Antonelli' - Norris not ruling out title fightback
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has not ruled out mounting a title fightback and says all the pressure is on Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

Norris claimed McLaren's first Grand Prix win of the season on Sunday with an impressive performance at the Hungarian Grand Prix and sits fifth in the Drivers' Championship, 91 points behind Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining.

Last year, Max Verstappen was 104 points off the championship lead with 10 events to go and fell just two points short of the title, which was won by Norris.

"The pressure is on him [Antonelli] for sure. There's no pressure on me. I've been feeling very confident," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

"They [Mercedes] have made more mistakes as a team and we have made less and we have come strong but I expect them to still win races and expect us to win more races. We just need to be perfect from here on now for the whole year.

"We need to improve the car still. We were certainly the quickest in Hungary from qualifying to the race. Not every race is going to be this simple, and we are going to be as quick, so we need to work hard to try to get the car to be this good to get the car to be this good everywhere. If we can, maybe that's a genuine question."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

McLaren brought a major upgrade packaged to Hungary, including a new floor, which has given them a big chunk of pace, having been able to fight at the front for most of the season.

Team principal Andrea Stella expects everyone to continue to bring new parts after the summer break, so McLaren must continue to improve too.

"Like it's always been in this 2026 season, it's a matter of a race of upgrades. The good news is that McLaren is now back in this race of upgrades, while fighting for the lead," he said.

"But I expect that the car that will be the best car at the end of the season will keep adding tenths of a second in the next 11 races, probably as much as half a second. So definitely a lot of work ahead of everyone, not only McLaren."

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship with 11 rounds remaining

Norris defends pit priority call in Hungary

Norris lost out to Piastri on the opening lap of Sunday's race and was stuck behind his team-mate, despite clearly having more pace in hand.

He eventually used that speed advantage around the second pit stop phase by running longer than Piastri and overcutting the Australian. Prior to that moment, Norris wanted to pit first and had stated on the radio he was "miles faster".

"I just want to win the race. There are certain rules we have as a team, and we can't harm each other's race by being overly aggressive and wanting to win," said Norris in the press conference.

"But I want to win, and I certainly had much better pace than him. We had a much better chance of winning the race, let's say.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris reacts to his first win of 2026 saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

"When I was stuck behind Oscar, Max was three or four seconds behind, and at that point he's still a threat. Ahead, there's no threat, and we have a lot more of a guarantee that we'll win as a team anyway.

"So, I wanted to box and undercut because my pace would have been so good, I could have pulled away a whole pit-stop window, I think, on him and boxed again if I needed to. Or I get him to box early. I think we were on the fine line between boxing too early and harming both of our races.

"So, it was just in the best interests of the team, which they rightly have to say back against me. But I want to do whatever I can to try and win a race, of course."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

Norris has generally had the upper hand over Piastri in recent races and many feel the British driver is performing just as well as last year when he became world champion.

The McLaren driver is unsure why his pace advantage was so significant in Hungary but hopes he continues to have the same feelings in the car after the summer break.

"The cars are identical, and I've just been feeling very strong lately. I've worked on many areas from last year," he said.

"I feel much more confident lately with how to extract performance, and I've worked a lot with my engineers to understand this car because it's certainly not an easy car to understand and figure out how to drive on the limit consistently.

"So, why? Just hard work. Hard work from my engineers and from myself to improve me as a driver and improve my driving. That is the answer."

Sports.title: What Arsenal's interest and Real's Diomande pursuit mean for Vini Jr
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior's Real Madrid future has been the subject of recent speculation, with Arsenal exploring a deal for the forward, but what could happen next?

What is the latest on Vinicius Jr?

Brazil star Vinicius Jr, 26, is entering the final year of his contract at Real Madrid.

Negotiations over an extension have dragged on without a breakthrough and it has caused increasing speculation over his future at the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Vinicius Jr's five best Real Madrid goals in LaLiga last season

That intensified last week when it emerged that Arsenal are interested in signing him this summer if he cannot agree a new deal at Real.

Meanwhile, Real Madrid have made a significant move for another winger - the exciting Ivory Coast international Yan Diomande at RB Leipzig.

It means doubts around Vinicius' future at the Bernabeu have grown over the past few days.

How serious is Arsenal's interest and can they afford him?

Arsenal's interest is real but in the early stages and conditional on a number of factors, not least the cost - which would be significant should the door open for Vinicius to leave Real.

There have been no club-to-club talks and there is no guarantee it progresses to a formal bid.

Arsenal, as newly-crowned Premier League champions, are looking to add another top-class forward despite signing Christos Tzolis. He was brought in to replace Leandro Trossard and there is doubt around the future of Gabriel Martinelli.

Last year they were keen on Vinicius's Real Madrid team-mate Rodrygo, while this summer Sky Sports News has reported their interest in Julian Alvarez and Morgan Rogers, who has since joined Chelsea from Aston Villa.

With one year left on his contract, the financial side of purchasing Vinicius would not be as severe as it previously has been - but it is worth remembering the sheer scale of an offer for the player two years ago from the Saudi Pro League.

Image: Vinicius Jr's stats from last season at Real Madrid

They were ready to pay him €1bn over five years and a transfer fee to Real Madrid of more than £300m (around €350m), which would have made him the most expensive transfer in history.

It would not cost anywhere near that much this time, but it gives a sense of what both Real and Vinicius were willing to forego in 2024.

Although the exact figure is confidential, Vinicius is believed to earn between €15m and €17m net per year. That's around £247,000 to £279,000 per week after tax. To earn that amount in the UK, Arsenal would need to pay him somewhere between £450,000 and £500,000 per week.

That would make him Arsenal's highest-paid player by far. Bukayo Saka is widely believed to be the current highest-paid, earning more than £300,000 per week.

A report in The Telegraph this morning claims Arsenal would be willing to go to £400,000. But that would still not equal Vinicius' current salary. Widespread reports in Spain claim that part of the current impasse with Real stems from his increased salary demands.

So is it just a dispute over a new contract?

Image: Vinicius Junior celebrates after scoring for Real Madrid in last season's Champions League clash with Manchester City at the Etihad

The situation has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest, further talks to come.

But there is no strong public evidence yet that Vinicius wants to leave Real Madrid for any reason, sporting or otherwise; no quotes, no interviews, no suggestive social media posts.

Real Madrid and - most importantly - new manager Jose Mourinho want him to stay and agree new terms. Sky Sports News reported on Monday morning that there will be further talks this week between Real and Vinicius' representatives, with Arsenal monitoring things closely.

Image: Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr is one of the most sought-after players in world football

Club president Florentino Perez is personally involved and has publicly expressed a desire for Vinicius to stay long term. Reports in Spain have long claimed that both parties have indicated a preference for him to remain at the club. Real Madrid do not want him to run down the deal into a free agent situation either.

Vinicius is more than just an outstanding left winger. He is a global superstar - and a Galactico in every sense. In that way he embodies everything about Real Madrid and fits right in.

Can the same be said about Arsenal? Signing such an icon has not been part of Mikel Arteta's Arsenal project so far, however exciting it might be to go in that direction.

What's the latest on Diomande?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande addressed speculation surrounding his future when he ws on World Cup duty - but Sky Sports' Jay Bothroyd is not convinced by the Ivorian winger

Real Madrid have upped their offer for winger Yan Diomande during talks with RB Leipzig, according to Sky in Germany.

They are reporting the offer, worth between £94m and £98m, has not been rejected yet, but further talks are required to satisfy Leipzig's demands.

According to Sky in Germany, around £102m is considered a realistic final price for Diomande, with Leipzig seeking a higher guaranteed fee from Real Madrid.

As things stand, there is no final agreement, but Leipzig are expecting the deal to be completed soon. Leganes have a sell-on clause for between five and eight per cent of the sale.

Diomande is at Leipzig and continues to train with the German club.

At the figures being discussed, Diomande looks set to become the most expensive African player ever, surpassing the £72m Arsenal paid for Nicolas Pepe in 2019.

Does Real Madrid's pursuit of Diomande impact Vinicius Jr?

Sky Sports News has been told Real's proposed deal for Diomande has no real bearing on the Vinicius situation. It says nothing about their desire to keep Vinicius, and only suggests they see a front three with both of these players in the team.

Diomande can play on the right wing as well, and he only strengthens the attacking options of the biggest club in the world.

According to Spanish newspaper AS, the players whose futures would be affected by Diomande's arrival are more likely to be striker Goncalo Garcia - who is wanted by Fulham - and winger Brahim Diaz. Rodrygo is still recovering from a long-term injury, so Diomande has space to come into the team quickly, even at only 19 years old.

What is the most likely outcome?

At this stage, all signs still point to Vinicius signing a new deal with Real Madrid. The fact that they will all meet again this week to discuss this suggests this is the direction of travel.

It will most likely come down to how closely Vinicius' earnings can approach those of Mbappe and satisfy his Galactico status in the squad. Normally, you do not say no to Real Madrid.

Real would not want to go into the new season with his contract running down and the resulting intensification of media speculation.

Arsenal's interest is likely to become more concrete only if the renewal fully fails, so this week is a crucial one.

Sports.title: Chelsea interested in Henderson after holding positive talks with Welbeck
Sports.content:
Chelsea are interested in signing Jordan Henderson from Brentford.

They are one of several big Premier League clubs looking to add his experience and quality to their ranks.

There is a realisation among those clubs that the 36-year-old has impressed at Brentford and with England since returning to the country from Ajax in 2025.

Brentford have been clear with Henderson since they signed him that they would not stand in his way if big clubs came in.

In that spirit, he could be allowed to leave on a free transfer, however that is not certain to be the case if multiple clubs come in. He has a year left on his Brentford deal.

Henderson has the character, leadership qualities and experience Chelsea are adding to their squad this summer.

Chelsea were keen on Granit Xhaka at Sunderland earlier this summer but a deal did not materialise.

Positive talks held for Welbeck

Image: Chelsea have held positive talks over the signing of Danny Welbeck

Chelsea have held positive initial talks with Brighton about a deal for Danny Welbeck.

With a year remaining on his contract, Brighton do not want to stand in the striker's way as long as they get a fair price for his sale.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Check out all 13 of Danny Welbeck's goals for Brighton in the 2025/26 Premier League season!

Welbeck has continued to be a reliable goalscorer in the Premier League at 35 years old. Last season he scored 13 times, after scoring 10 in the previous campaign.

His potential arrival would be another example of Chelsea prioritising physically imposing players with Premier League experience this summer.

They have already signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m - a record fee for a British player - and are close to bringing in Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix.

It would also place further doubt on the futures of strikers Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap and Marc Guiu.

Chelsea have signed several players from Brighton in recent seasons including their main striker Joao Pedro, plus Moises Caicedo, Marc Cucurella and Robert Sanchez.

A number of Brighton staff members have also moved to Stamford Bridge over the past four years, including sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Sam Jewell.

BlueCo's drastic change in transfer policy

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

Chelsea moving for a Brighton player is not out of the ordinary. However, Chelsea moving for a Brighton player in their mid-30s is.

Following that up with another from that demographic, despite them being currently injured, is a very deliberate ploy.

The BlueCo era has been defined by hoarding some of the best young talent on the planet and developing them in-house. That method has had some successes, but overall, it hasn't panned out.

There is clearly some recognition and accountability from the top brass about that. In bringing in Xabi Alonso as manager, they know they have lucked out in getting one of the most highly sought-after tacticians in the game. The Spaniard has clearly identified the need for experience and the club are following his lead.

The interest in Xhaka earlier in the summer were among the first signs of the shift. Even making a move for Maxence Lacroix is evidence of a change in approach.

The Welbeck move is surprising, but there is some logic that can be applied to it. Is he going to start every week? No. However, Chelsea's four senior strikers have an average age of just 23. Combined, they have made 269 Premier League appearances and scored 74 goals.

The Brighton veteran has 400 appearances and 90 goals on his own. To have that as your back-up to the young guns you want to develop makes sense.

Henderson? That's a complete 180 degree turn. Moises Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez are two of the more experienced players Alonso has. If you had to pick anywhere Chelsea needed a wise head, you wouldn't say midfield.

Yet, they wanted Xhaka. They now want Henderson. Alonso may have been the man to oversee the blossoming of players like Florian Wirtz at Bayer Leverkusen. However, he clearly sees the values of opposite characters and knows Chelsea, and perhaps more importantly, he needs people ready now.
