Sports.title: 'I don't even know what tomorrow looks like': Adam Ramsay-Peaty sends cryptic Olympics message after falling short of Commonwealth Games gold AGAIN as swimmer admits he has felt 'off' in Glasgow
Sports.content:
'I don't even know what tomorrow looks like': Adam Ramsay-Peaty sends cryptic Olympics message after falling short of Commonwealth Games gold AGAIN as swimmer admits he has felt 'off' in Glasgow

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Adam Ramsay-Peaty dunked his head under the water, looked up at the scoreboard and smiled. His time, 26.94 seconds, was only enough for bronze but he did not beat himself up about it.

Throughout his career, Ramsay-Peaty has swum with the spirit of the giant lion tattooed on his bulging bicep. These Glaswegian waters will duly confess that age can tame the most vicious of animals.

‘My superpower looks very different now,’ said the 31-year-old, who was slow off the blocks and needed every dose of muscle memory to pull his way back into third.

‘Juggling babies with milk and having a toddler around is a different superpower. As a professional athlete, yeah, I’m still committed. I’ve been that person that wins all the time and it costs you pretty much everything. I wouldn’t say it’s worth it now.’

The killer instinct has been replaced by parenthood.

Peaty remains Britain’s best breaststroker but he does not fill international opponents with fear like he used to. The sands of time catch up with everyone.

Most swimmers peak in their early 20s. Even the great Michael Phelps, with his 6ft7in wingspan and size 14 feet, did not win another Olympic medal after the age of 31.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty reacts after winning bronze in the men's 50m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games

His wife Holly was seen watching on as Ramsay-Peaty secured his second medal of the Games

Ramsay-Peaty, pictured with wife Holly, had earlier labelled sport 'cruel' in an emotional statement

Ariane Titmus won four Olympic golds and here, aged 25, she is standing poolside with a microphone, carrying out post-race interviews for Australia’s national broadcaster.

Ramsay-Peaty’s finish time was almost a whole second off his world record. He accepted his bronze medal with grace, waving to his adoring Glaswegian audience, and he was more interested in taking home the cuddly unicorn for his son.

‘For me, that period of time when I was undefeated for eight years, or whatever it was, it was athlete first and then human,’ he said. ‘Now it’s human first and then athlete. That’s a good gamble. We don’t really know what the outcome’s going to be. We obviously need to switch up what we’re doing in training to a certain extent. I’ve been in my new training base 12 weeks so let’s keep it in perspective.’

Two lanes to his right, Scoland’s Archie Goodburn was swimming with terminal cancer. Doctors found three inoperable brain tumours two years ago and his presence offered a dose of perspective for the man whose life has turned into a swimming pool soap opera.

There is nothing glamourous about competing in Glasgow. Events finish late and start early in what feels like a tarted-up leisure centre. Sleep is a luxury. Ramsay-Peaty has been catching the double decker bus to Tollcross with his fellow swimmers. Single fares on the local First Bus service normally cost £2.45. No VIP shuttles here. With no road closures, the traffic tends to bottleneck at the turning off Wellcross Road, allowing plenty of thinking time

After missing out on gold over 100m on Saturday night, Ramsey-Peaty questioned the sacrifices required for this life. “What’s the point of all the 5.30ams? What’s the point of all the metres every day? What’s the point of feeling exhausted all the time? What’s the point of saying, “No” to all the family events because of training?” Time will tell how strong his appetite remains for mouthfuls of chlorine.

Ramsay-Peaty spoke of the importance of fatherhood as he and Holly expect their first child

The legendary British swimmer took to social media with a lengthy statement on Monday

The 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, at least, offer a more glamorous proposition. The swimming meets will be staged at the SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, which most recently hosted the World Cup quarter-final between Spain and Belgium. The 100,000-square-foot NFL field will be transformed into the largest swimming venue in Olympic history. Perhaps the idea of a family trip to the West Coast to watch dad’s final race will make it all worthwhile.

‘There’s been a lot of learning this week,’ he said. ‘

‘I said it in Birmingham but this is absolutely my last Commonwealths. I just went out there and enjoyed it – really enjoyed it – but we just weren’t fast enough, weren’t good enough. We have to look at why, because the data this season has been tracking on an upward trend.

‘I can’t really put my finger on it, where I just lost that power to the stroke. Something’s not kicking but I’ve got to learn from it. To get two bronzes, with a relay to go, I’d say that’s success. I’m not going to be too hard on myself, not anymore.’

Earlier, on TNT Sports, he admitted: 'I don't even know what tomorrow looks like really, there's a lot of learning. I've felt 'off' this week and I don't know why. We are trying new things.'

This is not the fastest pool on the swimming circuit. Most modern elite Olympic swimming pools are three metres deep but the waves in this shallower, two-metre basin can add a few tenths of a second to finish times.

Ramsay-Peaty’s comments after his 100m race on Saturday night raised eyebrows among some of his peers. He claimed he deserved more. He felt his input – physical and mental – warranted more than a third-place finish. Several athletes accused him of arrogance and entitlement. They wake up just as early and train just as hard, but last night it felt like he had been away for a reality check.

When the adrenaline is still pumping through his body after races, Ramsay-Peaty sometimes says things he regrets. He can be unfiltered. His post on Instagram before the race was perhaps more measured. ‘I know this story won’t be filled with glory, victory and gold,’ he wrote. ‘However I’ll keep fighting, learning, adapting and striving for excellence until I can no longer give anymore. Sport isn’t a fairytale if your happiness and self-worth are only validated by medals. But it can be, if you find value in the hardship, the struggle and the tough times which might ultimately lead you to what you seek.'

He spent Sunday morning scribbling notes in his hotel room in Glasgow. ‘Am I good enough? Am I not good enough?’ asked the monkey in the back of his mind. He is now chasing the pack – as well as his younger self – yet he remains one of sport’s greatest showman. When the Chinese, American, Dutch join him in the pool, the chase will not get any easier.

Sports.title: Italian football in CHAOS as Paolo Maldini and Leonardo QUIT after Andrea Pirlo was blocked from becoming new national team coach amid links to Russian betting firm
Sports.content:
Italian football has been rocked by the news that Paolo Maldini and Leonardo have quit in the wake of Andrea Pirlo being ruled out of the running as next national team boss.

Pirlo is no longer in the frame to become Italy's next manager after 'political' concerns were raised over the football legend's sponsorship deal with a Russian betting company.

Pirlo, 47, was backed by former team-mate and new Italian Football Federation (FIGC) technical director Maldini to land the role after legendary ex-Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola reportedly declined the opportunity.

The former AC Milan and Juventus star was on the brink of agreeing a deal with the crisis-hit football nation before several Italian politicians raised concerns about Pirlo's role as an ambassador for Russian betting firm Fonbet.

It was felt Pirlo, who had been prepared to leave his current job as coach of Dubai United, should not have conflicting views on Italy's support for Ukraine in the war with Russia.

In the subsequent fallout, Maldini and his assistant Leonardo are reported to have stepped down, too, after just 16 days in their jobs.

Pirlo himself confirmed that he was no longer in the running in an Instagram post on Monday, urging that his Fonbet deal was linked to his job in the United Arab Emirates and is 'exclusively for commercial and sports' purposes.

His claim has been refuted by Dubai United owner Sergey Lomakin, who stated that Pirlo's involvement with the firm was not an involuntary aspect of his deal.

Andrea Pirlo is no longer in the running to become Italy's next manager after a dramatic twist

The Italy legend's appointment has been blocked after 'political' concerns were raised over his sponsorship deal with Russian betting company Fonbet in the United Arab Emirates

Pirlo said in a statement: 'In recent days, I have witnessed with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking on the role of Head Coach of the Italian national team.

'Out of respect for the institutions, the Federation, and all those involved, I have chosen to remain silent until now.'

'However, I feel it is my duty to clarify certain aspects.

'Throughout my career, first as a player and now as a coach, I have always conducted my activities in full compliance with the laws of the countries in which I have worked and the contracts I have signed.

'The professional collaboration at the centre of the recent controversy arose as part of my career in the United Arab Emirates and is exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature.'

It is understood Maldini was furious by the decision made by FIGC president Giovanni Malago and quit his role as technical director after Pirlo's appointment was blocked.

Adverts, endorsements and sponsorship deals pertaining to betting are strictly prohibited in Italy.

Pirlo added: 'Attributing political meaning to this collaboration means attributing to me beliefs I have never expressed and that are not mine.

'I would like to thank Maldini and Leonardo for the esteem and trust they have shown me. I know their expertise, their seriousness, and the love they have always dedicated to Italian football.

Paolo Maldini was furious at the decision and has decided to walk away from his role as a result

'I regret that a sporting decision was quickly dragged into a public debate that ended up attributing to me meanings and intentions that are not mine.

'My love for Italy does not depend on a position. It is part of my history, my identity, and will continue to accompany me, always.'

Pirlo was at best a third-choice after Carlo Ancelotti and Guardiola turned down offers to coach a team that has failed to qualify for three consecutive World Cups.

Now former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini and Antonio Conte are back being discussed for the job.

Sports.title: Vinicius Junior stays AWAY from Real Madrid training as transfer saga rumbles on: Arsenal target skips pre-season return date amid contract stand-off - with Spanish giants making stance clear
Sports.content:
Arsenal target Vinicius will not return to Real Madrid training this week as doubts over his future rumble on.

The Brazil winger was knocked out of the World Cup at the last-16 stage and with new manager Jose Mourinho laying down the foundations for his second spell in charge of the club the expectation in Madrid was that Vinicius’s could return before the end of the month.

But the player is staying away while his representatives try to revive talks over an extension to his contract that runs out at the end of this coming season.

Madrid’s position is that the player’s future is in his own hands. If he lowers demands to be joint top earner with Kylian Mbappe he will stay.

But if he does not the 15-times European Cup winners have no plans to make an improved offer and the way will be left clear for Arsenal.

Vinicius Jr has not returned to Real Madrid pre-season training amid his contract stand off

New Madrid boss Jose Mourinho had expected the Brazilian to return to training this week

In a move seen as an illustration of that intention not to fold to the players’ will, Real Madrid moved closer yesterday to making their 100m euros capture of Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig official.

The player, represented by the same Roc Nation agency as Vinicius, gives Mourinho yet another attacking option in an already over-populated forward line.

The Daily Mail Sport understands Roc Nation’s talks with Real Madrid will centre on Vinicius’s huge commercial worth to the club.

The player’s current contract means he gives around 50 per cent of publicity-deal revenue to them, during the World Cup he had lucrative deals with 15 multinational sponsors – a number topped only by his international team-mate Neymar.

The 26-year-old has the same representatives as Diomande, who was also on Arsenal's radar, and there has been interest from Saudi Arabi over the past 12 months.

Vinicius is one of a number of forward targets Arsenal are exploring, with Julian Alvarez, Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola also of interest.

Liverpool are considered favourites for Barcola but his situation could change if PSG fail to land Diomande with Madrid leading that charge and trying to close the deal quickly.

He is in the final year of his contract and if an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling, rather than lose him for free next summer.

The deal would represent a sensational coup for Arsenal if they were successful but the clubs are still to open official talks.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

Vinicius Jnr has scored 128 goals across eight seasons in Madrid, and narrowly missed out on the Ballon d'Or to Rodri in 2024.

Daily Mail Sport has reported that Gabriel Martinelli is up for sale as Mikel Arteta looks to add more firepower to his forward line.

Leandro Trossard has already been sold to Besiktas, while Arsenal confirmed the signing of Greek winger Christos Tzolis for £34million from Club Bruges on Thursday.

Sports.title: Do YOU think you could beat Luke Littler at darts? The world No 1 is inviting amateurs to take him on in new Netflix show... for a prize of £501,000!
Sports.content:
Do YOU think you could beat Luke Littler at darts? The world No 1 is inviting amateurs to take him on in new Netflix show... for a prize of £501,000!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Luke Littler is inviting fans to try to beat him in a leg of darts for an eye-watering prize of £501,000.

The Professional Darts Corporation (PDC) world No 1 will star in a one-off live Netflix show on October 30, taking on 20 punters from across the nation.

Regional qualifying heats in London and Manchester are already open for sign-ups.

'Everyone thinks they can beat me,' said Littler, perhaps overestimating the public's self-confidence a tad.

'Now they get a chance to prove it. Bring it on.'

The lucky darts players who get a chance will be hoping to catch the 19-year-old on a bad day, but the prospect of that is vanishingly thin.

Luke Littler is inviting fans to play him at darts for a £501,000 prize live on a Nteflix show

The 19-year-old is aiming to complete a clean sweep of the eight PDC ranking events - but YOU could be a thorn in his side

Littler defended his World Matchplay title in scintillating style last week, averaging a record of 111.04 across the tournament. The previous record was set by Phil Taylor with 106.31 in 2010.

In the final against Gerwyn Price in Blackpool, Littler stepped up his game, averaging a devastating and record-breaking 111.53, winning 18-9.

The Nuke is aiming to complete the clean sweep of the eight PDC ranking events this year, something which has never been done before.

He is on course for that so far after winning the World Championship, World Masters, UK Open, and World Matchplay.

But he will need to take part in some Pro Tour events in order to qualify for the Players Championship Finals in November. Unfortunately, that means a family holiday in Spain will have to be sacrificed; Littler is needed in Leicester.

Littler boosted his bank balance by £225,000 after beating Price, taking his total winnings in the PDC's two-year Order of Merit to £3,143,500.

'It's been a crazy week, one of the best weeks of my life with the darts I've played,' Littler told Sky Sports after his World Matchplay triumph.

Littler was emotional after winning the Premier League against Luke Humphries in May

'It's been tough. The stats may look like it's easy, but when you're on this stage with how hot it is, it's not easy.

'I've definitely played some of the best darts of my life. I feel like it's the best version of myself. I have just played so well.'

Defeated finalist Price, the world No7, said: 'Luke is one in a million. I think I played pretty decent.

'In that game I missed a couple of opportunities but the bull checkouts, the 167, it was a big turning point even though it was early in the game.

'I didn't play brilliant, but I played decent.'

Littler has faced boos during some events and admitted that he almost walked away in the final of the Premier League Darts against Luke Humphries as a result.

‘After Brighton, I came off stage, and then in Manchester I was sat at home saying to Faith [Millar, girlfriend], “I don’t want to do it any more”. Just the crowd every week.

‘I said to her, “I’m down bad”.’

The teenager then had to stop speaking as he welled up with emotion, before Humphries added: ‘It shows what it means to us as players. Being on the road for 16 or 17 weeks - it’s hard work.’

Sports.title: 'It was a s***show': Sean Dyche hits out at Everton's transfer strategy and says he was 'constantly putting out fires' before he was axed - and reveals why Andoni Iraola's 'lower league style' has landed him the Liverpool job
Sports.content:
Sean Dyche has labelled Everton's transfer strategy during his time at the club as a 's***show', while he has lauded new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola's management skills.

Dyche, speaking on The Good, the Bad and The Football podcast, reflected on his near two-year spell at Everton when discussing transfer windows.

The 55-year-old highlighted the difference between his long spell at Burnley where he was able to delegate recruitment with staff aware of his priorities and demands.

By contrast, Dyche explained he needed to become more involved in the recruitment process during his time at Everton, where the Toffees had been in the midst of a financial crisis as the club battled to stay in the Premier League.

'When you are at somewhere a longer period like I was at Burnley, after year three or four we have got it up and running, it is working, everyone knows their roles,' Dyche told Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt.

'You can delegate better, once that trust builds and you are onto something, the CEO, data analysts and sports science knows what you are thinking, then it is really easy.

Sean Dyche claimed he was 'constantly putting out fires' at Everton with the club a 's***show' during his time in charge

'It is not so easy going to Everton, where it is like a f***ing s***show you know and it is constant putting out fires.

'It was a whole different ball game, brilliant in a weird way, rewarding when you get it done.

'There was a reward because you get the feeling of "I've played that little part in a really important time" and Evertonians now treat me way different than at the time.

'When I came out they were ready for me to go, but when I meet fans now they are like "thanks for helping us through it".'

Beto and Youssef Chermiti were Everton's only signings in the summer of 2023 where the club paid a fee, with Ashley Young joining on a free transfer and Arnaut Danjuma and Jack Harrison joining on loan.

Moise Kean and Alex Iwobi were among players to generate sizeable fees after being sold the same summer.

The following summer saw Everton sign Iliman Ndiaye, Jake O'Brien and Tim Iroegbunam in fee-paying moves, with Harrison, Jesper Lindstrom, Orel Mangala and Armando Broja joining on loan.

Amadou Onana was a significant summer departure with the midfielder joining Aston Villa in a £50m move.

Dyche has lauded new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola as he complemented him for adapting his tactics to fit the Premier League

Dyche was sacked a month after the Friedkin Group completed their takeover of the club, with David Moyes appointed as his successor in January 2025.

This was followed by an overhaul of Everton's recruitment staff in June, with the appointments of a technical director, director of scouting and recruitment, a head of football strategy and analytics, and head of player trading.

After his success in guiding Burnley into Europe was compared by Scholes to Iraola's achievement last season at Bournemouth, Dyche revealed what impressed him about the Spaniard since moving to the Premier League.

Dyche highlighted how Iraola had adapted to the Premier League after a slow start, with the new Liverpool boss having quickly realised his intended style of play at Bournemouth was unlikely to yield results.

Iraola had seen his Bournemouth side thrashed 3-0 by Everton in October 2023, with his team failing to win any of his opening eight matches in charge.

Dyche pinpointed a major shift from Iraola towards 'lower league football' with higher quality players after that initial spell, with the Spaniard overseeing three impressive seasons at the club.

Dyche suggested Iraola had played 'lower league football at a high level' during his time at Bournemouth

'Iraola basically plays lower league football, but at a high level. They turn you and turn you, and force you into submission,' Dyche said.

'High quality and high energy version.

'I marvelled at it because we ran all over them at Everton when he was trying to play what you would imagine is the Spanish way.

'I think he is brilliant at managing, as you could tell he went "this ain't going to work".

'The next time we played them, he is bombing it down our throats, getting us turned, full backs keep turning and having to run back towards their own goal, centre halves thinking that they never get a break.

'They looked a different outfit and he's done a brilliant job.'

Sports.title: Inside Jeff Bezos' bid to buy into Liverpool: The role the Amazon billionaire could play, what 'super smart' £1.35bn investment means for transfer business, how it affects FSG - and what happens next
Sports.content:
Inside Jeff Bezos' bid to buy into Liverpool: The role the Amazon billionaire could play, what 'super smart' £1.35bn investment means for transfer business, how it affects FSG - and what happens next

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

As soon as the news emerged that Jeff Bezos was interested in forming part of a consortium to buy a stake in Liverpool FC, the jokes began.

Anfield was to become the Amazon Arena, a nod to the company where Bezos made his fortune. New signings would arrive on next-day delivery. Liverpool would not just be competing to be champions of Europe but the galaxy, referring to Bezos's part in the 21st-century space race.

Whatever your opinion on the fourth-richest man in the world, it is hard for Reds fans not to dream of the endless possibilities under a man worth £190billion according to Forbes.

But will Liverpool actually see any of the proposed £1.35bn investment? What role, if any, will Bezos play? And is it time for those supporters to get excited?

Daily Mail Sport has spoken to sources on both sides of the Atlantic to help tackle some of the big questions…

Jeff Bezos has discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool

Liverpool are in a period of transition with Andoni Iraola taking over as head coach in June

What is going on?

Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group are in talks to sell a stake in the club to a consortium backed by Amit Bhatia and funded in part by the family of steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal.

Bezos is interested in being part of the consortium and other names are also keen to get involved.

Bhatia will be in charge of the bid. He stepped down as co-owner and director of Championship side Queens Park Rangers on Tuesday after nearly two decades at Loftus Road, where he has a stand named after him.

The 46-year-old is the son-in-law of Mittal, the 73rd richest man in the world with £23.4bn to his name per Forbes, and the consortium is keen to buy around £1.3bn in the club.

A spokesperson for Liverpool's owners FSG told Daily Mail Sport earlier this week: 'An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.'

It is thought that FSG welcome the potential opportunity and this is another way the conglomerate, who also own the baseball behemoth Boston Red Sox, are looking to further position the club for success.

It would be a similar move, though on a larger scale, to when FSG sold 4 per cent to Dynasty Equity in September 2023. Principal chair John W Henry has always been eager for additional investment while still being keen to hold the majority stake.

FSG sources stress that no deal is signed just yet, with the parties in early discussions at this stage, though the fact the consortium has been put together is a significant development. And there are signals that everyone involved is keen for a deal to be done.

Businessman Amit Bhatia is part of the consortium in talks to buy a stake in the Reds

Would it be a wise move for FSG?

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire certainly thinks so.

He tells Daily Mail Sport: 'As far as the potential Liverpool investment is concerned, it looks like it's going to be up to 30 per cent or £1.3bn. That values the club at just over £4bn, which is broadly in line with expectations.

'From FSG's point of view, it's a super smart piece of business. Yes, they have sold part of the club before but this will ensure they still own a controlling stake of around 60 per cent.

'So in terms of the long-term strategy of the club and the individual transfer windows and recruitment issues, it is still FSG's decisions that are being made. If they are selling 30 per cent, that money goes to FSG not Liverpool, so there is no physical impact upon the club's coffers.

'If the club is looking to borrow money at a future date for whatever circumstances and you are owned by Mittal's son-in-law and Bezos, they will be in a position to lend money on an interest-free basis which can only help in terms of cash flow.

'Also, having a potential partner of the magnitude of Bezos does mean there is the opportunity for synergies. If Amazon Prime want to increase their global influence, then one way could be to do a partnership with Liverpool, whether in terms of content or sponsorship.

'Liverpool goes out to the world and Amazon goes out to the world as well. As well out of the world, maybe! He is flying people into space after all.'

Finance experts believe it would be 'a super smart piece of business' from FSG to sell a stake in the club

What is Bezos's involvement?

Bezos, who made his massive wealth by founding Amazon out of his Seattle garage in 1994 and has since launched ventures such as (the unfortunately-named, for Liverpool fans) space company Blue Origin and the Washington Post news group, is interested.

Sky News reported that Bezos was invited to join the syndicate led by Bhatia. His exit from QPR on Tuesday, the same day the news broke about his interest to invest in Liverpool, came at a telling time.

The intentions of the consortium are clear, though Bezos has historically been cautious when it comes to major sports deals. He was interested in buying the current Super Bowl winners Seattle Seahawks and fellow NFL team Washington Commanders but pulled out.

There has been an influx in similar deals in recent years, notably Ineos' investment in Manchester United and Todd Boehly with Clearlake at Chelsea.

While Boehly is still seen as the figurehead of that move, Behdad Eghbali and Clearlake run the show. Eghbali loves football and has been pleasantly surprised at the English sporting culture when attending games at Stamford Bridge.

Perhaps we will see Bezos in the posh seats at Anfield before too long, too.

It is believed that Bezos was invited to join the syndicate led by Bhatia

What happens next?

The news of FSG being open to selling a stake came as a surprise to many, including some personnel at the club.

It is not said to be an indication that Liverpool's Boston-based owners, who bought the club in 2010, are looking to sell up. If anything, it is part of their strategic plan to position the club to prosper.

Some fans point the finger at FSG for various shortcomings.

They are no saints, for sure – some of their ticketing policies and price hikes have irked many – but they have done far more good than bad during their time as custodians of the club, including regenerating Anfield and financially backing the club into a successful era on the pitch.

As for the consortium, sources believe they are serious.

The day-to-day running of the club would be unlikely to change if it goes through, but being backed by such mega-rich investors can never be a bad thing.

Sports.title: First Danny Welbeck, now Jordan Henderson! Chelsea plot deal for England veteran, 36 - with Blues also closing in on move for Brighton star, 35, after he scored 13 Premier League goals last season
Sports.content:
First Danny Welbeck, now Jordan Henderson! Chelsea plot deal for England veteran, 36 - with Blues also closing in on move for Brighton star, 35, after he scored 13 Premier League goals last season

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Jordan Henderson on a free transfer from Brentford.

After missing out on Sunderland’s Granit Xhaka, the Stamford Bridge club have moved for 36-year-old Henderson to fulfil a role on the pitch and crucially in the dressing room.

As Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed, Chelsea are already closing on a move for Danny Welbeck as manager Xabi Alonso looks to add older heads to a young squad.

Alonso has determined that the squad dynamic needs to change to help Chelsea achieve their goals and maintain a successful challenge to rivals.

There are a number of clubs interested in Henderson, who is still recovering from a fractured arm suffered during the World Cup, including two other Premier League sides, but Chelsea are favourites to sign him.

Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Brentford veteran Jordan Henderson

It comes after Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed talks with Brighton's Danny Welbeck

Earlier on Monday, Daily Mail Sport revealed how 35-year-old Brighton striker Welbeck has emerged as a player of interest within Stamford Bridge, and is now a contender to join the Blues squad under Alonso.

Welbeck has scored 46 goals in 176 games in the Premier League for the Seagulls, having previously played for Manchester United and Arsenal, among others.

Chelsea currently have five strikers on their books in Joao Pedro, who is considered untouchable, Emmanuel Emegha, Liam Delap, Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

The Blues have been looking at sales or loans to trim down their options up front.

Welbeck scored 13 times in the league for Brighton in 2025-26, and was considered unfortunate not to make the England squad under Thomas Tuchel.

Joao Pedro and Delap are currently on Chelsea’s pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, with Emegha absent due to injury. Jackson is not involved due to his run at the World Cup with Senegal and Guiu has not been selected.

Welbeck joined Brighton in 2020 and triggered a one-year contract extension in March. If he moves to Stamford Bridge he would add to the lengthy list of signings Chelsea have made from Brighton in recent years - including Marc Cucurella, Moises Caicedo, Robert Sanchez and Joao Pedro.

Sports.title: Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood

The 23-year-old will ride at Group race level for the first time with rides on unbeaten two-year-olds in Tuesday's Vintage Stakes and Wednesday's Molecomb Stakes

View 3 Images Kaiya Fraser: has his first Group ride on Dr Rascal at Goodwood (Image: Maureen McLean/Shutterstock)

Kaiya Fraser is not letting a vicious attack from a horse sabotage his rise up the riding ranks.

‌



The 23-year-old was bitten by a rival runner at Ascot earlier this month, leaving a hole in his breeches, and knocked to the ground. But he dusted himself off, remounted Dr Rascal and calmly steered the unbeaten Oliver Cole-trained colt to his second victory.

‌



“Of course it hurt, you saw me rolling on the ground,” said Fraser, recounting the Ascot incident. “It hurt a lot and left a bruise on my thigh. The bruising has gone now and there is a bit of a scar there.

‌



“I was lucky to get up after and ride the winner a couple of minutes later.”

Dr Rascal will be one of the horses Fraser is set to ride at Glorious Goodwood this week, in today’s Vintage Stakes, during what will be the biggest week of his career so far.

The Rebecca Menzies-trained Adonius in the Molecomb Stakes, who has won three on the bounce, is his other stand out mount.

‌



View 3 Images Kaiya Fraser is hauled off his mount as Mr Twig attacks him (Image: At The Races)

“It’s my first time in Group races so I am obviously excited and I am on two unbeaten horses,” he said.

“Obviously they are going to have to step up again in this company and then we can really see how good they are and where they stand in the top company.”

‌



The 23-year-old has followed an untypical path into horse racing, having been born and raised an Eastender, in Hackney, London.

His late grandfather Winston, who loved a bet, piqued his interest in the sport and he gained his first experience of horses from a volunteering stint at the Ebony Horse Club in Brixton.

Aged 16, he enrolled on an apprentice course at the British Racing School in Newmarket, got his first job with the now retired Chris Wall, and now works for Harry Eustace.

‌



View 3 Images Kaiya Fraser: won on Adonius at Chester (Image: PA)

Despite losing his claim last season Fraser is well on course to improve on his best annual score of 45 wins, having shown his preparedness to travel from home in Newmarket to wherever winners can be found

He added: “I ride a lot for Rebecca and had to travel all the way up to Musselburgh to ride him first time out and again second time out.

Article continues below

“Then I went to Chester and now I’ve got the chance to ride him in a big race. That shows that when you put in the work, you get the best out of it.”

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty secures another Commonwealth bronze in 50m breaststroke
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty secures another Commonwealth bronze in 50m breaststroke

Adam Ramsay-Peaty scored a bronze medal in the men's 100m breaststroke earlier this week and the Team GB athlete has managed to follow that up with another medal

View 2 Images Adam Ramsay-Peaty has been competing at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow (Image: Getty Images)

Adam Ramsay-Peaty secured bronze once again in the 50m breaststroke semi finals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games as Sam Williamson claimed glory.

‌



The Brit was quickly up against it after the start but his late charge wasn't enough to see him bag another hold. He finished in 26.94 - 0.44 off the Australian winner, who was able to back up his 100m performance to secure an incredible double in Glasgow.

‌



Michael Houlie secured second as Ramsay-Peaty finished third by just 0.01. Ramsay-Peaty came into the race as defending champion having won gold four years ago in Birmingham and revved up the crowd during his walk-in, but it wasn't enough to inspire him to glory.

‌



He said: "It is quite disappointing in terms of the time and as we know times equal medals. I felt I could have been a little quicker but I need to look at it and see where it is going on because nothing makes sense this week to be honest.

Adam Peaty doubles down on family feud as he shares how he copes with tough times READ MORE :

"I am working way too hard. If those results were how much I am working then they would be a lot better. I need to look at that and adjust course because we are sailing in some rough seas right now and it is not sustainable. I have come back from worse and we will see where we end up."

The goal remains a medal at the Olympics in Los Angeles in 2028 but Ramsay-Peaty insists he's happier in himself than when he was dominating the sport.

‌



He said: "Evolution of the man I guess. I came in 2014 and was a young boy, had no responsibilities and all I cared about was my car. Now I am an older man, married, one kid George and also another on the way. Not even comparable where I am now. I am much much happier and now the performances need to catch up."

View 2 Images Adam Ramsay-Peaty secured bronze in the Men's 100m Breaststroke (Image: Getty Images)

He had booked his place in the final with a time of 26.82 seconds, as he finished behind just South Africa's Houlie in his semi-final.

‌



It comes after the Olympian secured a bronze at the weekend in the 100m breaststroke final, despite going in as the fastest qualifier.

He was beaten by Williamson and Jersey history maker Filip Nowacki. His time - 59.65 seconds - was more than four-tenths slower than his semi-final swim and three seconds off his personal best from seven years ago.

He cut an emotional figure afterwards, but his comments have divided opinion after Ramsay-Peaty claimed he "deserved more" after all his efforts after several years away.

Article continues below

He said: "It took a lot of courage to get back into the sport, so we should be happy with everything we get, but then that contradicts the athlete inside me and what I work for.

"I just think I deserve more. I know sport isn't about what you deserve or even what you work for - it's who gets it on the day. I just know I'm a better athlete than that. It's very disappointing."

Sports.title: Man Utd enter advanced talks for striker transfer with £30m clause proposed
Sports.content:
Man Utd enter advanced talks for striker transfer with £30m clause proposed

Joshua Zirkzee could be set for a loan move away from Manchester United this summer having struggled to convince at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee has never convinced Manchester United fans (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Juventus are holding advanced talks with Manchester United over a loan deal for Joshua Zirkzee. The move would also include a £30million option to buy for the Italian outfit.

‌



The striker has been strongly linked with an Old Trafford departure this summer, but is keen to secure a place in Michael Carrick's plans. The Dutchman has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter during his time in with the Red Devils - unable to break into Ruben Amorim's plans or Carrick's since joining the club under Erik ten Hag in 2024.

‌



The 25-year-old has netted just five goals in 56 Premier League outings for United. The Red Devils are said to be receptive to Zirkzee's departure this summer, though the former Bayern Munich prospect is understood to be happy to stay.

‌



Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits READ MORE :

It is suggested that he feels European football at United in 2026/27 will provide him with greater chances under Carrick. The Netherlands international sought to leave in January but was informed by United that it would not be feasible.

Nevertheless, The Sun now suggest a transfer could be possible with Serie A club Juve in advanced negotiations. The Turin side appeared poised to capture France international Kolo Muani from Paris Saint-Germain following his underwhelming loan stint with Tottenham Hotspur last season.

However, Juventus have reportedly failed to reach an agreement on a fee with PSG after talks broke down. It is understood that the Italian club have swiftly turned their attention to Zirkzee as they seek a new frontman.

‌



Juventus are said to be the most serious suitors for Zirkzee, though Roma have also harboured a long-standing interest in the striker. Luciano Spalletti's outfit are reportedly the frontrunners for his signature, having moved considerably quicker in negotiations.

View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee has transfer interest from Juventus (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Zirkzee is no stranger to Italian football, having spent one season on loan at Parma and two seasons turning out for Bologna. The Dutchman is understood to view Serie A as a far more suitable tactical environment for his style of play.

It is claimed that Zirkzee's camp have responded favourably to Juventus's advances. United are also reportedly prepared to sanction a loan deal with a £30m purchase option, despite having splashed around £36.5m to bring him to the club two years ago.

The report further states that club officials acknowledge the fee is a reasonable reflection of his worth, given his inability to produce consistent performances.

Article continues below

Zirkzee caught the eye in United's 5-0 pre-season victory over Rosenborg last Friday. Yet his showings in the Premier League have left much to be desired.

The Dutch forward currently finds himself behind both Benjamin Sesko and Mateus Cunha in the pecking order at M16, and Marcus Rashford's potential return to the fold could push him even further down the ranks.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest

Arsenal are keen on landing Vinicius Jr and the Brazilian will remain away from Real Madrid as his representatives continue to negotiate with the Spanish side - who want him to lower his demands

View 2 Images Vinicius Jnr's future at Madrid remains unclear (Image: Getty)

Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr will not return to training this week as his contract talks rumble on with Arsenal waiting in the wings.

‌



The Brazilian has been given an extended break having played at the World Cup, but will not return before the month is out despite there being an expectation that he would be back in the Spanish capital for pre-season.

‌



Vinicius is staying away while his representatives try to make progress in talks over an extension to his contract, which will run out at the end of the upcoming season. Real do not want to let him leave for free, and there is a scenario whereby they will cash in.

‌



Arsenal are waiting to see how the saga plays out and the major issue with Los Blancos and their player stems from his wage demands. Vinicius wants financial parity with top earner Kylian Mbappe, but the La Liga giants want him to lower that request, reports the Daily Mail.

If he fails to do that then the door opens for the Gunners, who have internally discussed signing the 26-year-old but no bid has yet been tabled.

Vinicius Junior's next club odds as Real Madrid star linked with move to Arsenal READ MORE :

Arsenal can offer Vinicius Jr key non-negotiable that Real Madrid cannot after transfer update READ MORE :

Jose Mourinho is back in charge at Real following his initial stint from 2010 and 2013 and had a public spat last season involving Vinicius. The Special One has wasted no time in bolstering his squad, adding the likes of Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konate and Marc Cucurella.

‌



Real are now closing in on the £115million signing of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, one of the most in-demand wingers of the summer. PSG had looked like his most likely destination but they refused to match his financial demands and the Spanish giants are ready to break their own transfer record to land the Ivorian.

Diomande, who scored 12 goals and registered eight assists last term, would serve as a replacement for Vinicius if he does make a move to the Bernabeu.

View 2 Images Real Madrid have reportedly agreed a deal to sign RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande, who could replace Vinicius Jnr (Image: (Photo by Stuart Franklin/Getty Images))

‌



Teams in Saudi Arabia are also monitoring Vinicius' situation closely after months of speculation linked him with a switch to the Middle East. Arsenal are known to want more quality in the final third and Vinicius more than fits the bill.

Arsenal want a left-sided attacker and have just missed out on Morgan Rogers, who chose to move to Chelsea. BBC Sport claims that the Brazilian is viewed internally as the club's number one target and any move would almost certainly be a club-record deal.

Sports.title: Danny Welbeck interest signals outbreak of Chelsea's new common-sense approach
Sports.content:
Danny Welbeck interest signals outbreak of Chelsea's new common-sense approach

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has given the green light for the club to have talks with Brighton over the acquisition of the experienced England striker

View 4 Images Danny Welbeck looks likely to be leaving Brighton for Chelsea (Image: Izzy Poles/AMA)

Since making his debut as a 17-year-old Manchester United player early in the 2008/09 season, Danny Welbeck has made 525 club appearances and 42 appearances for England. It is a fair number but not excessive in a career spanning 18 seasons.

‌



Unfortunately, Welbeck has had several lengthy injury lay-offs, missing a total of around two-and-a-half years’ football since suffering a serious knee problem in May 2016. At times, it has been very tough going for the very likeable striker but if you wanted to see a positive side to those struggles, it could be said that for a 35-year-old Premier League forward, he does not have too many miles on the clock.

‌



Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

In scoring 13 Premier League goals last season, he looked to be in prime condition. If Chelsea manage to get him to Stamford Bridge from Brighton, they will not be signing a striker who is ready for a lap of honour.

‌



Welbeck turns 36 in November but will fancy at least two or three more seasons at the top level in this country. Welbeck was slightly unfortunate not to get the shout from Thomas Tuchel for the World Cup.

He must have been somewhat aggrieved to have found Ivan Toney ahead of him, that is for sure. And he will feel there are plenty more miles on the clock, especially as he knows he will not be a guaranteed starter wherever he plays football in the coming seasons.

View 4 Images Morgan Rogers has been Xabi Alonso's big signing of the summer so far (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



If Chelsea and Brighton can come to an agreement over Welbeck, who has a year left on his deal, the only issue is whether the player himself thinks it is a good move. This is a club whose last ‘permanent’ manager lasted three and a half months, and whose transfer policy has been pretty unfathomable over the past few years.

In comparison, Brighton is a bastion of stability and finished above Chelsea in last season’s Premier League table. But Chelsea now has a blue-chip manager in Xabi Alonso.

View 4 Images Liam Delap could be on his way out of Stamford Bridge after a difficult first season (Image: Chelsea Football Club/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



In Morgan Rogers, their marquee signing of the summer is a proven - yet still developing - Premier League performer. Chelsea are one of the clubs trying to sign free agent John Stones.

There is an outbreak of joined-up transfer thinking at The Bridge. Welbeck, of course, will be a squad man. And his numbers and attitude will mean he is an excellent squad man.

In his time at United, Sunderland, Watford, Arsenal and Brighton, Welbeck has made 400 Premier League appearances, scored 90 goals and made 32 assists in those games. Not startling numbers, but useful.

Article continues below

View 4 Images Chelsea are among those hoping to sign free agent John Stones (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

He is an attacker who knows what it takes to be effective in the Premier League. Liam Delap looked like that sort of striker at Ipswich Town but scored once in the Premier League for Chelsea last season.

If and when the Welbeck signing is confirmed, it is unlikely to get Chelsea fans out of their seats but it is a sensible move from Alonso. And sensible and Chelsea haven’t always been on the same page in recent times.

Sports.title: Chelsea star hails Xabi Alonso's plan with parting dig at Enzo Maresca's style
Sports.content:
Chelsea star hails Xabi Alonso's plan with parting dig at Enzo Maresca's style

Xabi Alonso is the latest man in charge of Chelsea and his style has quickly left a mark on Levi Colwill, who believes he has release the shackles seen under previous managers

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has just taken charge at Chelsea

Chelsea's Levi Colwill has hailed Xabi Alonso's style of football as he took a swipe at his former bosses who had been "really rigid".

‌



The defender spent most of last year on the sidelines after suffering a serious knee injury in pre-season, restricting him to only four outings across a campaign that saw the Blues have three different men in the dugout - Enzo Maresca, Liam Rosenior and Calum McFarlane.

‌



Alonso is the latest man to take on the hot seat at Stamford Bridge and the ex-Liverpool boss arrives with some serious pedigree. He claimed the Bundesliga title whilst in charge at Bayer Leverkusen, breaking the stranglehold Bayern Munich had on the German top flight.

‌



His style of play aided Leverkusen as they won the double and he's been quick to get those ideas across during his early weeks at Chelsea - with Colwill praising his principles when compared to those who've come before him.

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Chelsea outline Pedro Neto stance as Man City and Liverpool consider offers READ MORE :

He said: "Xabi wants free flowing football, I've had a lot of managers who are really rigid and want you in right positions, but with him, play what you see, find the space and exploited it at a fast pace."

The Blues finished tenth last term after a dire season but Colwill believes the squad have it in them to mix it with the champions. He said: "I feel like the players we've got in our team are ready to do that. With having a manager of this quality now, when it all comes together we're definitely going to be able to challenge and push for the Premier League."

‌



Chelsea have not won the Premier League since 2017 and, under their BlueCo ownership, they've only finished in the top four once. Alonso has refused to go public with any major targets and has suggested that things may not click as quick as some hope.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca and Mauricio Pochettino are the only two managers Levi Colwill has consistently played under

"I don't want to talk too early about what's our goal," he said. "We want to have a good season. We want to deserve to be as high as possible, and for that we need to work hard. We need to develop this team with new players, new coach, new ideas. Sometimes it takes longer, sometimes it happens quicker.

Article continues below

"So be ready to try to develop this idea that we have, this plan. But so far, good feeling. Good energy. The players are working hard, and that's what we want."

Sports.title: England to play two of seven Euro 2028 matches away from Wembley in best-case scenario
Sports.content:
England to play two of seven Euro 2028 matches away from Wembley in best-case scenario

England will co-host Euro 2028 with Wales, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland

View 2 Images England are set to play the majority of their Euro 2028 matches at Wembley Stadium (Image: PA Wire)

England may have to play just two matches away from Wembley Stadium at the European Championships in 2028 if they make it all the way to the final. Thomas Tuchel's side will be among the favourites to win the tournament as hosts and having finished third at the recent World Cup.

‌



The Three Lions still have to qualify for the competition, as per new UEFA rules which means only two of the host nations will qualify for the tournament. England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will all have to navigate the usual qualifying campaign.

‌



If any of the nations fail to qualify, then the two country's with the highest qualifying rank will take one of the backup spots. It means that in a worst-case scenario, the two highest ranked nations are still guaranteed a place.

‌



Pep Guardiola's telling reasons for rejecting Italy job as England learn stance READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Northern Ireland had been in contention to host the tournament with the rest of the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland, but it failed to secure the £400million funding to bring Casement Park up to scratch.

Games will be held across nine different venues in eight cities, in London at Wembley Stadium and Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, The Etihad Stadium in Manchester, the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, St James' Park in Newcastle, Villa Park in Birmingham, Hampden Park in Glasgow and the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

‌



If England qualify for the tournament, they'll play their first game at the Etihad Stadium, before two games at Wembley Stadium. Should they qualify at the top of their group, they'll likely play their round of 16 clash at St. James' Park in the only two games to be played on the road.

View 2 Images Euro 2028 will take place in the UK and Ireland (Image: James Manning/Getty Images)

Each of the four host nations will host a quarter-final tie, with the Three Lions clash still on home soil in the North East of England. England will then return to Wembley Stadium for the quarter-final and semi-finals, with the showpiece finale also held at the home of English football.

‌



Unlike the recent World Cup, fans will be able to watch the majority of games, with kick-offs at normal times throughout the tournament.

The tournament itself will get underward on will kick off on June 9, 2028, with the curtain raiser at the Prinicpality Stadium in Cardiff, running for a month until July 9, 2028, with the final at Wembley.

There'll be 24 teams qualify for the tournament, with four nations in six groups, playing a total of 36 matches over 12 days - a stark difference compared to this summer's World Cup.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd boss wanted to re-sign Danny Welbeck as Chelsea open transfer talks
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd boss wanted to re-sign Danny Welbeck as Chelsea open transfer talks

Chelsea have opened talks with Brighton to sign Danny Welbeck, who could've returned to boyhood club Manchester United had a former Red Devils manager got his way

View 2 Images Danny Welbeck was linked with a return to Manchester United (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Manchester United blocked Erik ten Hag's attempt to sign Danny Welbeck in 2024 - and now the veteran striker could end up at rivals Chelsea. The Blues have opened talks with Brighton to sign Welbeck, who's still banging in the goals at Premier League level aged 35.

‌



The former United star is understood to be keen on a move to Stamford Bridge. But Welbeck could've returned to Old Trafford a couple of years ago, with Ten Hag pushing the Red Devils to re-sign him as a replacement for Anthony Martial.

‌



Ten Hag had seen Welbeck's ability first hand, having tormented United in the Dutchman's very first game in charge two years prior. His goalscorer record, impeccable fitness and leadership qualities appealed to him.

‌



But Ten Hag didn't get his wish. According to The Athletic, United discussed signing Welbeck after Ten Hag's recommendation, but they ultimately didn't make an offer during what was a summer filled with changes above Ten Hag, with his own future uncertain at one stage.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits READ MORE :

7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season READ MORE :

Welbeck addressed the report during an interview with The Times a few weeks later. "It's speculation and there's always that link for me because I've been at the club," he explained. "As I said, I'm just focusing on what I can control myself and all the other stuff is pretty irrelevant."

‌



The Red Devils' focus turned to signing younger players, with Benjamin Sesko arriving last summer at the age of 22. United have been linked with signing an experienced striker this summer but nothing has materialised, with Michael Carrick's three signings coming in goal and midfield.

As for Welbeck, he's set to join Xabi Alonso's Chelsea. The ex-England international, who was tipped for a World Cup call-up this summer, scored a career-best 13 league goals last season.

Should Manchester United hijack Chelsea's move for Danny Welbeck? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Erik ten Hag wanted to sign Danny Welbeck (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

United legend Gary Neville reckons that Welbeck should never have been allowed to leave Old Trafford, having been sold by Louis van Gaal to Arsenal for £16million in 2014. "Danny Welbeck, to be fair, should never have been let go at United," Neville affirmed on the Stick to Football podcast.

"If you've got a squad of 24, 23, and you want to keep five or six strikers, he's got to be one of those. You've got to keep him."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
