World.title: Iraqi Islamic Resistance rejects Saudi drone attack claims
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Islamic Resistance in Iraq has rejected Saudi accusations that drones used in attacks on the Kingdom were launched from Iraqi territory, calling the claims an attempt to deflect attention from Yemen’s military operations.

In a statement issued on Monday, July 27, 2026, the group denied Saudi allegations and warned that any military action by Riyadh would be met with what it described as a “harsh response.” The statement dismissed Saudi claims that Iraq was the source of drone attacks targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

According to the group, the accusations are intended to justify Saudi Arabia’s inability to respond to what it called “painful Yemeni strikes” against the Kingdom’s infrastructure. The group also accused Saudi Arabia of using the allegations to divert attention from the ongoing conflict in Yemen.

The Islamic Resistance in Iraq warned that any “reckless” Saudi action would face severe retaliation. It also urged Saudi Arabia to end what it described as the blockade on Yemen instead of directing accusations at Iraq. The statement concluded by accusing Riyadh of attempting to cover up its failures and shift blame for the attacks.

The statement came shortly after Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi ordered Iraqi security agencies to investigate Saudi claims that drones targeting the Kingdom had originated from Iraqi territory. The investigation follows official accusations made by Saudi authorities earlier on Monday.

Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Defense announced that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed several drones attempting to target oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

The ministry claimed the drones were launched from Iraqi territory by what it described as Iran-backed militias, adding that the Kingdom reserves the right to respond “at the appropriate time and place.”

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the attack and called on the Iraqi government to prevent its territory from being used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries.

The exchange of accusations comes amid heightened regional tensions and follows a series of attacks affecting energy infrastructure and shipping routes across the Gulf.

While Saudi Arabia has blamed armed groups operating from Iraq, the Islamic Resistance in Iraq has categorically denied responsibility and warned against any retaliatory measures. The Iraqi government has not announced any preliminary findings from its investigation.

World.title: Iraqi National Security Adviser: Three Iranian-backed factions have handed over weapons
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi says three armed factions have already begun handing over their weapons to the Iraqi state, revealing new details about Baghdad’s discussions with both the United States and Iran over restricting weapons to state control.

Speaking in an interview with journalist Zainab Rabie, Al-Aboudi said he was unsure whether Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi would approve of him disclosing some of the details. Al-Aboudi said previous Iraqi governments had attempted to place all weapons under state authority but had been unable to fully implement the policy.

He explained that recent understandings with the United States regarding the withdrawal of American forces by September 30 have removed one of the main justifications used by some armed groups to retain their weapons.

According to Al-Aboudi, three factions have already started handing over their weapons to the state, describing the move as an important step toward consolidating security under government control. Al-Aboudi said Baghdad held discussions with both Washington and Tehran because some armed groups maintain ideological and political ties with Iran.

He revealed that Iranian officials pledged to support Iraq’s efforts to limit weapons to state institutions after becoming convinced that U.S. forces would withdraw according to the agreed timeline. “I believe there will be no weapons outside the state’s authority once the U.S. withdrawal is complete,” Al-Aboudi said.

The National Security Adviser also disclosed that Iraqi officials raised objections during talks in Tehran over previous Iranian strikes targeting the Kurdistan Region. He said Baghdad made it clear that attacks on Iraqi territory were “unjustified and unacceptable under any pretext.”

Al-Aboudi described Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s recent visit to Washington as a turning point in Iraq-U.S. relations. He argued that Iraq had been “almost isolated,” even regionally, before the visit, while the United States viewed Iraq with suspicion.

According to Al-Aboudi, the meetings shifted the relationship toward an economic partnership, encouraged major American companies to reconsider investing in Iraq, and helped revive U.S. interest in the country.

He added that both sides also agreed to resume military training programs that had previously been suspended, continue security coordination, and discuss the issue of Iraqi detainees transferred from Syria, with Baghdad receiving what he described as positive responses from Washington.

Al-Aboudi’s remarks come just days after government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi stressed that limiting weapons to state control is a sovereign Iraqi issue and should not be negotiated in foreign capitals.

The comments coincided with Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran, where he discussed energy, trade, transportation, agriculture, and broader regional developments with Iranian officials.

World.title: Iraq orders probe into alleged drone launches targeting Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi ordered a probe on Monday into Saudi Arabia’s accusation that drones targeting the kingdom were fired from Iraqi soil, threatening legal measures against anybody found to be guilty.

The decision came two days after Saudi Arabia’s Defence Ministry said that it intercepted and destroyed drones fired from Iraq by Iran-backed militias targeting installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province and the capital, Riyadh.

According to a statement issued by his office, Al-Zaidi directed security officials to analyze the intelligence given by Saudi Arabia and establish if Iraqi land was utilized to conduct the assaults.

The government said that it remained dedicated to preventing Iraqi land from being used as a base or transit route for attacks on neighboring nations and that individuals found to have engaged in such crimes would be prosecuted in accordance with the inquiry results.

Baghdad also underlined its commitment to maintaining tight relations with Saudi Arabia, characterizing the two nations’ relationship as founded on mutual respect, similar interests, and good neighborly relations.

The inquiry comes at a crucial moment for Al-Zaidi, who is scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia for discussions with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman after previous travels to the United States and Iran to enhance Iraq’s economic and diplomatic ties.

The reported drone launches have highlighted one of the most challenging issues for Al-Zaidi’s administration as it seeks to attract foreign investment while maintaining state authority over armed groups that operate outside the government’s direct supervision.

Iraq’s Prime Minister has frequently said that its territory would not be used to threaten neighboring nations, as Baghdad aims to strike a balance with Iran, the United States, and Gulf Arab countries while presenting itself as a regional center for commerce, investment, and transportation.

World.title: Iran, US hold fire as Saudi Arabia intercepts drones
World.content:
Tehran – Iran and the United States held their fire for a third consecutive day on Monday, though American ally Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted a drone attack launched by Tehran-backed groups in Iraq.

Fighting between the longtime foes has paused since early Saturday after 13 nights of renewed US strikes on the Islamic republic sparked by a breakdown in diplomacy over Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

President Donald Trump’s UN envoy had suggested the pause was to give negotiations a chance, but Tehran said there were no direct talks with the US to end the conflict, which began in late February with a wave of US-Israeli strikes and has rocked both the region and the global economy.

“Mediators may convey messages from the American side to us regarding current developments in the region. But at present, we are not engaged in any negotiations with the United States,” said Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei.

Trump told US media outlet Axios that mediating countries had asked him to hold fire, adding: “We are in very deep talks with Iran”.

“If they don’t work out, we will go back to very strong military action,” Trump said, warning he would not wait long for diplomacy to succeed.

Despite the lull, Saudi Arabia came under attack on Monday, with its defence ministry saying it had intercepted several drones fired by Iran-linked groups in Iraq targeting oil facilities.

No group claimed responsibility, but Riyadh called on Baghdad to prevent such attacks from being launched from its territory.

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels also said they launched drone attacks on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure in response to incursions by the kingdom’s drones. Riyadh is yet to comment on the claim.

Saudi Arabia and other Gulf nations accused pro-Iran militias in Iraq of launching waves of attacks on their territory during the conflict’s earlier phase, but the groups haven’t claimed any attacks in the region since the resumption of hostilities.

Elsewhere, the Israeli military, which has not joined the recent fighting, said it had intercepted two drones near the Jordanian border and was investigating where they had been launched from.

– ‘Mafia gang’ –

Global stock markets rallied and oil prices tumbled on Monday after the pause in strikes between Washington and Tehran.

It came as respite for Gulf shipping and the oil industry, with international benchmark Brent dropping more than four percent to $87 a barrel.

Control of the Strait of Hormuz remains a hurdle to any peaceful resolution, and Iran insists on managing the crucial conduit for oil and gas.

Its powerful Revolutionary Guards have been stopping vessels trying to transit the trade route in recent days, including six that state television on Monday said had sailed outside Iran’s designated route.

Tehran says it has held talks in recent days with Oman, which also borders the strait, on “common principles and operational mechanisms” to ensure the safe passage of shipping.

In June, Muscat and Tehran said they would discuss imposing service fees, a move Washington opposes.

But Muscat also angered Iran after saying vessels could transit the Hormuz strait via its waters, with Tehran responding by attacking ships.

Iran’s foreign ministry on Monday said the United States was not involved in the recent discussions with Oman.

Instead Baqaei criticised Washington, saying its conduct in recent years has “resembled that of a mafia gang that adheres to no rules or laws”.

“So long as such behaviour by the United States continues, we cannot be hopeful about the emergence of a reasonable process,” he said.

World.title: Uptime Institute signs Nineveh deal to support Iraq’s digital infrastructure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Uptime Institute, located in the United States, has inked a deal with Iraq’s Nineveh governorate to promote the development of digital infrastructure and enhance the region’s technology industry, adding to a wave of US investment promises made during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington.

The memorandum of agreement, signed during the U.S.-Iraq Business Summit held by the US Chamber of Commerce, intends to assist Nineveh in developing digital infrastructure that meets international standards while also assisting Iraq’s larger efforts to modernize its economy and attract foreign investment.

The collaboration aims to strengthen digital infrastructure resilience, transfer technical skills, and cultivate local talent to assist future technological initiatives in the northern governorate.

Nineveh Governor Abdul Qader al-Dakheel said that the cooperation will help establish the groundwork for economic development and position the governorate as a hub for technological investment.

Uptime Institute, a New York-based firm that creates worldwide standards and certifications for data centers and digital infrastructure, announced that it would collaborate with Nineveh to boost the region’s digital capabilities and promote the construction of robust, sustainable infrastructure.

The arrangement was one of over 50 commercial partnerships revealed during the U.S.-Iraq Business Summit, when American and Iraqi firms disclosed projects spanning energy, aviation, finance, manufacturing, technology, and infrastructure, totaling more than $60 billion.

The digital infrastructure plan represents Iraq’s rising attempts to diversify its economy away from oil by increasing investment in technology, telecommunications, and data infrastructure while producing higher-skilled private-sector employment.

As restoration efforts continue, Nineveh actively seeks international investment to repair infrastructure, boost economic development, and position itself as a regional center for technology and creativity, despite the serious destruction of its city Mosul during the battle against Islamic State.

World.title: Drone strikes rock Sudan’s El-Obeid after army secures highway
World.content:
Berlin – Drone strikes blamed on paramilitary forces shook the Sudanese flashpoint of El-Obeid on Monday, hours after the army regained control of the city’s highway to the capital Khartoum.

The army’s rival, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), have for months amassed troops around El-Obeid, attempting to encircle it ahead of an apparent large-scale assault.

Following a days-long advance across North Kordofan state, the Sudanese army on Sunday managed to push the RSF west, off the 400-kilometre (250-mile) highway that connects Khartoum with the embattled Kordofan region’s largest city, two army sources told AFP Monday on condition of anonymity.

Drone strikes were reported on the city at dawn, with local officials attributing them to the RSF.

The local lawyers’ association and a branch of the Agricultural Bank of Sudan were left in ruins, an AFP reporter saw, though no casualties were reported.

Since the start of the year, drone strikes by both forces have killed more than 1,000 people in Kordofan alone, according to the UN.

Since April 2023, the war between Sudan’s army and their one-time allies the RSF has torn the country apart and killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate.

It has also created the world’s largest displacement and hunger crises, with over 33 million people in need of humanitarian aid.

For months, each side has sought to cut off the other’s supply lines around El-Obeid, which sits at an important crossroads.

Its north-south highway runs from Khartoum through Kordofan to the southern border, while its east-west axis connects RSF strongholds in the Darfur region to army-controlled central and eastern Sudan.

– Breaking a stalemate? –

“Now the militia has to turn to defend West Kordofan, which is the front line for Darfur,” a retired army officer told AFP.

The highway to Khartoum remains closed to civilians, who have for most of the war relied entirely on the eastern road to the White Nile, where the RSF regularly launches deadly drone strikes.

The army advance “opens a second supply route to El-Obeid and beyond”, said one of the army sources.

Inside the city, where the UN says hundreds of thousands are in need of aid, relieved El-Obeid native Sabreen Mohamed told AFP that “the highway opening means goods can flow”.

Praising the army’s advance in North Kordofan, Mohamed brushed off the RSF’s dawn drone strikes as “death throes”.

“We’re used to it, every time the army advances, they retaliate against North Kordofan,” she said.

Though both sides have reportedly committed war crimes including indiscriminate bombing, the army is generally regarded more favourably by civilians who have faced a litany of horrors at the hands of the RSF.

As the RSF mobilised on El-Obeid, the UN has for weeks warned of a repeat of atrocities committed during the RSF’s takeover of the Darfur city of El-Fasher in October last year, which a UN inquiry found bore the “hallmarks of genocide”.

A city of about half a million people, which the UN says has doubled in size because of displacement, El-Obeid has been caught in the crossfire since the war began.

It was under paramilitary siege from April 2023 until February of last year, when the army broke through.

Ever since, RSF attacks on roads, neighbourhoods and critical infrastructure such as power stations have worsened a humanitarian crisis, where the UN says only a fraction of the city has reliable access to food.

World.title: Pirlo bitter over debate that cost him Italy coaching job
World.content:
Rome – Former Italy playmaker Andrea Pirlo, who was favoured for the national coaching post, expressed his bitterness on Monday over the debate which has led to him no longer being a candidate.

The 47-year-old had, to many Italian fans’ surprise, become the favourite to be tasked with reviving the national side’s fortunes after they failed for the third successive time to qualify for the World Cup.

He had benefitted from Spanish great Pep Guardiola declining an offer.

Despite the latest setback, Giovanni Malago, president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), said later on Monday that the new coach would be named “soon”.

Whilst Pirlo had a stellar playing career — including being a key member of the 2006 World Cup-winning side — his coaching CV is short on success.

A contract with a Russian betting firm had only added fuel to misgivings, with several Italian politicians saying over the weekend that his appointment would be inappropriate.

“(I) learned yesterday evening that I am no longer a candidate to be coach of the national side,” Pirlo wrote in a post on Instagram, adding that he felt the need to “clarify certain points”.

– ‘Great bitterness’ –

According to Italian media, he was due to be named this week despite his only trophy success since turning to coaching in 2020 being a single Italian Cup.

Presently coach of United Arab Emirates side Dubai United, he failed to deliver when in charge of Juventus — for whom he had sparkled as a player — Sampdoria and Turkish outfit Karagumruk.

Pirlo said in his post that he was angry at being judged not on his sporting record but on the wider issue over his links to Russia.

He and fellow 2006 World Cup winner Marco Materazzi had taken part in May at an event held by the betting firm in the Luzhniki Stadium in Moscow, signing autographs.

“I have followed with great bitterness the debate surrounding my candidacy,” he wrote, whilst thanking Italy’s technical director and former AC Milan teammate Paolo Maldini and his advisor Leonardo for their “esteem and confidence (in him)”.

“I regret that a decision which is based on sporting criteria rapidly became a public controversy, in which intentions and ideas which do not reflect my personality were attributed to me.”

According to Italian media, whilst Leonardo and Maldini preferred Pirlo to the prickly but significantly more successful Antonio Conte, newly-installed federation chief Malago had been against the appointment from the start.

Conte — who has won the Serie A title with three different clubs and also the Premier League with Chelsea — is back in the frame for the job of coaching the Euro 2020 champions, according to la Gazzetta dello Sport.

Conte, who turns 57 on Friday, previously coached Italy from 2014-16, guiding the Italians to the Euro 2016 quarter-finals where they lost to Germany on penalties.

Maldini is apparently threatening to resign, after just three weeks in the job, if either Conte or another former national coach Roberto Mancini, who coached them to Euro 2020 success, is appointed.

The former AC Milan and Italy legend’s preferred choice now is Brazil-born former Italy international Thiago Motta, who has coached Bologna and Juventus, amongst other clubs.

World.title: US dollar slightly falls against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar declined on Monday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,499.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,500.5 Iraqi dinars on Monday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,505 Iraqi dinars and 1,495 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,501 and 1,500 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: India summons Ukraine envoy for ship attack, Kyiv seeks talks
World.content:
Unacceptable and must be avoided: MEA

NEW DELHI: India summoned the Ukrainian ambassador Monday to condemn attacks on commercial shipping, underscoring the adverse impact of such attacks on the safety of maritime navigation, freedom of navigation and international commerce.However, Ukraine claimed it had warned India about the growing threats to civilian navigation from Russia's actions in Black Sea, saying the only sustainable way to restore maritime security was to increase international pressure on Russia to end its attacks on civilian shipping. In a statement, the Ukrainian embassy here also sought dialogue between the foreign ministers on the Black Sea security situation.Ukrainian ambassador Oleksandr Polishchuk was summoned by the MEA in connection with the attack on the commercial vessel MV Omorfi that resulted in the death of an Indian national. The ministry said it conveyed its serious concern over the incident and condemned such attacks on commercial shipping in the strongest terms."The ambassador was requested to convey to the Ukrainian authorities India's strong concerns over the targeting of commercial vessels and reiterated that such actions, which endanger the lives of innocent civilian seafarers, are unacceptable and must be avoided," the ministry said.The attacks by both Russian and Ukrainian forces on commercial shipping have caused the deaths of five Indian seafarers. In the latest such attack, a merchant vessel carrying four Indians was struck at Ukraine's port of Odesa. While two Indian crew members were confirmed safe, information about the other two is awaited.Ukrainian embassy here said in a statement that foreign minister Andrii Sybiha had written to his counterpart S Jaishankar expressing sympathy for the families of Indian seafarers who lost their lives as a result of the deteriorating security situation in the Black Sea."We hope that, following the relevant proposal made by the minister of foreign affairs of Ukraine, a conversation between the foreign ministers of our two countries will take place in the nearest future to discuss in detail the current security situation in the Black Sea region," the Ukraine statement said.According to the embassy, Ukraine had consistently warned its international partners, including senior Indian officials, about the growing threats to civilian navigation arising from Russia's actions in the Black Sea."Ukraine has also informed its partners about the measures it is taking to prevent the delivery of military cargo and disrupt logistical routes used to sustain Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine," it said.The embassy also said that timely and preventive action by competent authorities was vital to protecting seafarers, ensuring the safety of civilian navigation, and strengthening international maritime security in regions where such threats were clearly identified.

World.title: End to Parliament impasse in sight, Lok Sabha may take up bill on exam reforms today
World.content:
NEW DELHI: On a day the opposition's protest over Delhi Police's alleged excesses against protesting students washed out proceedings in both Houses of Parliament yet again, signs emerged that normalcy may return from Tuesday, with government's bill for enhancing punishment in cases of paper leaks likely to be taken up for discussion in the lower House.

Sources said a breakthrough emerged following Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's outreach to both government and the opposition for breaking the impasse that has persisted since the monsoon session began on July 20, and that a discussion on the Vande Mataram bill, which makes insulting the national song a penal offence, may begin in Rajya Sabha.

What also seems to have nudged the opposition to allow a discussion on Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, which was introduced by Union minister Jitendra Singh amid din, was government's determination to push through its passage with a voice vote without a debate.

It has also brightened the prospect of government revisiting its move to amend the women's reservation law and increase seats in LS and state assemblies through a constitution amendment bill provided its hectic efforts to reach two-third majority in Parliament succeed.

With government determined to secure passage of the public exams bill, Congress and its allies ran the risk of losing a chance to articulate their criticism, while BJP-led NDA would have used the opportunity to back its claim that leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi and other opposition functionaries were running away from a debate.





The bill is part of a raft of measures announced by PM Modi to pacify students protesting the NEET-UG paper leak and related issues, and Birla repeatedly emphasised the salience of discussion as the matter was linked to youth and the public exam process. Around 2pm, he told both opposition and government to sort out their differences before the House met again at 5pm.

Sources said he met Congress's K C Venugopal and Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav, and also reached out to other opposition members, nudging them to agree to a debate.

While six hours have been allotted for discussion, the time may be extended if the House wanted, he said, urging the opposition to choose discussion over the disruption it was causing by demanding a response from home minister Amit Shah over allegations of police excesses.

Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju noted that 91 amendment notices to the bill had been moved by opposition MPs and this suggested their willingness to join the discussion.

Even as the two sides inched towards a resolution, they continued to trade charges in LS, with opposition insisting that Shah respond to the charge that police used excessive force, including pellet guns in Delhi, and AK-47 in Bihar, against protesting students. Opposition said Shah needed to come out of hiding and face Parliament.

Govt, however, matched the aggression and accused Congress of being obstructive for partisan reasons. "The image of Congress has fallen. Don't do anything to further damage your reputation," Rijiju said.

World.title: Ayodhya Ram mandir donation row: On Supreme Court suggestion, temple SIT to include a forensic auditor
World.content:
During the last hearing, the bench had warned petitioners against politicising the issue

NEW DELHI: The UP government on Monday immediately accepted Supreme Court's suggestion for inclusion of a chartered accountant having expertise in forensic audit in the three-member SIT, constituted on the Supreme Court's July 20 order to investigate alleged embezzlement of donations to Ayodhya Ram mandir managed by Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.As soon as a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought to know the UP govt's view on inclusion of a chartered accountant having expertise in forensic audit in the SIT headed by IGP Kiran S, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said, "Without taking instructions from the govt, I am assuring the court that such an expert will be drafted into the SIT."The bench said, "We want an expeditious, fair and transparent investigation into all aspects of allegations relating to alleged misappropriation of donation funds for the temple managed by the trust."Appearing for a PIL petitioner, advocate Devadatt Kamat said since there were allegations of siphoning out of donations meant for temple construction from across the country, the trust should be asked to upload all receipts of donations on its website."This will help devotees identify whether their donations for construction of the temple and thereafter have been accounted for or not," Kamat said and requested the court to entrust supervision of the SIT probe to a retired Supreme Court judge.The SG objected and said, "We must trust the Supreme Court and three honourable judges who are monitoring it."The CJI-led bench turned down Kamat's request and said, "When we are monitoring the probe being carried out by the SIT, there is no need of any supervision by a retired judge. The SIT will transparently investigate all aspects of allegations relating to siphoning of funds." It asked the SIT to submit a probe status report in two weeks.During the last hearing, the bench had warned petitioners against politicising the issue and assured that there would be fair, impartial, transparent and expeditious investigation by the SIT. Supreme Court said if the SIT experienced any impediment from any quarter in carrying out the investigation, it should approach Supreme Court without loss of time.

World.title: Supreme Court: No bail in digital arrest cases barring exceptional grounds
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Monday said it is against grant of bail to anyone accused of being part of digital arrest scams, except when they point out "extraordinary grounds" which warrant their release from custody.

Sending out a message to HCs and trial courts, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "Digital arrest scams are worst kind of crime against people, especially senior citizens whose life savings and hard-earned money are fraudulently siphoned out when they need it the most."

When an accused pleaded that he had only helped the main accused in opening a bank account and that he has been in custody for more than a year, the bench said this made him an accomplice in the crime.

âEquate digital fraud cases with robbery, dacoityâ

Rejecting his bail plea, the bench said, âIn cases related to digital arrest, we will not grant bail unless extraordinary grounds exist.â

On Friday, the bench had said that police and investigating agencies must invoke stringent anti-organised crime law provisions against those found involved in digital arrest or cyber fraud cases. It had also said, âDigital arrest and cyber fraud cases must be equated with robbery and dacoity.â





Last year, Supreme Court had taken cognisance of digital arrest cases mostly targeting senior citizens, tasked CBI to probe cases pan-India, and was instrumental in activating an inter-departmental mechanism involving different agencies to devise and implement steps to curb the menace. As per probe agencies, people have been cheated of Rs 3,000 crore through digital arrest and cyber heists.

World.title: Coast Guard airlifts ailing seafarer from ship off Gujarat coast despite rough seas, adverse weather
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A seafarer was airlifted to safety off the Gujarat coast after the

carried out a difficult medical evacuation despite rough seas and adverse weather.

In a post on X, Indian Coast Guard said that it âsuccessfully executed a MEDEVAC of a 21-year-old seafarer from MT Murlikisan off

on 26 July 2026. With a swift response from MRCC Mumbai, CGDHQ-1 Porbandar swung into action, providing immediate telemedical assistance while deploying surface and air assets.

The patient was airlifted using an ICG Advanced Light Helicopter to Porbandar, medically stabilised by ICG doctors, and shifted to Hospital for further treatment.â

The seafarer was reported to be suffering from acute chest pain and a high fever, requiring urgent medical attention.

The helicopter successfully winched the patient from the vessel and transported him to the Coast Guard Air Enclave, where an Indian Coast Guard medical officer provided initial stabilisation. Officials said the successful evacuation underscores âICG's steadfast dedication to maritime safety and reflects the spirit of Vayam Rakshamah (We Protect).â

A few days ago, the Coast Guard evacuated a 29-year-old Indian mariner suffering from a medical emergency aboard the tanker 'MT Kashimasan' off the Goa coast, transferring him ashore for urgent treatment.

World.title: 'No legal action, FIRs being withdrawn': Bihar govt assures protesters in big win for students, CJP
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bihar government on Monday announced the withdrawal of FIRs against all protesters who were arrested for alleged involvement in last week's violent protests over the NEET (UG) issue in the state.

According to the Bihar government's home department, the relief would apply to all cases registered up to 6 pm on July 26, a day after the demonstrations.

The home department further stated that those arrested within this period would be released and no further action would be taken against any of the accused.

The announcement came hours after the Bihar Police, while detailing the violence during the demonstrations, stated that 694 people â nearly half of them minors â were detained for allegedly attempting to enforce a state-wide bandh last week over the NEET paper leak issue.

According to the statement, violence during the July 25 bandh, called by Left-wing students' unions, left 91 personnel and officials, two administrative officers and 13 civilians injured.

Among those detained, "339 minors and students" were released after age verification, while the remaining 355 were produced before courts and were facing proceedings "for involvement in violent activities."

Thirteen government vehicles were vandalised and another was set on fire by bandh supporters.





Those injured in the incidents included the SP of Siwan and SDPOs from Siwan and Sitamarhi districts.

In Saran, two Block Development Officers (BDOs) suffered grievous injuries, with one losing an eye and the other sustaining a serious head injury.

Both BDOs were "battling for life" at separate hospitals in Patna, the state capital.

Cockroach Janta Party warns of fresh protests



Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the youth outfit that led protests in Delhi over the NEET (UG) paper leak issue, on Monday warned the Centre of renewed demonstrations if cases against protesters across the country were not withdrawn.

The withdrawal of cases was one of the CJP's three conditions for calling off its agitation, which it ended on July 25 after the Centre accepted all its demands.

The CJP had been holding an indefinite protest since June 21, seeking accountability over the paper leak issue. On July 20, a march to Parliament organised by the outfit turned violent, leaving protesters and security personnel injured.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: 47 GW battery storage, 23 GW pumped storage projects in pipeline
World.content:
Representative AI-generated image

NEW DELHI: India has nearly 47 GW of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity at various stages of development as the country ramps up storage infrastructure to support rapid expansion of renewable energy and meet rising electricity demand, power ministry informed Parliament Monday.As of June 30, nearly 16 GW of BESS capacity was under construction, about 12 GW awarded, while another 19 GW is at the tendering stage, MoS for power Shripad Yesso Naik said in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. On the pumped storage front, 16 GW of projects are under construction, while another 7 GW has received concurrence and is awaiting construction.As per National Electricity Plan (Generation), India is projected to require 47 GW of battery energy storage capacity and 27 GW of pumped storage capacity by 2031-32. The minister said large-scale deployment of storage systems will be critical for integrating renewable energy, meeting peak electricity demand and ensuring grid reliability.The minister also said India will require investments of about Rs 4.8 lakh crore in energy storage infrastructure by 2031-32 to support the growing share of renewable energy in the power mix. Of the total investment, about Rs 3.5 lakh crore is estimated for battery energy storage systems and Rs 1.3 lakh crore for pumped storage projects.The storage push comes alongside an aggressive capacity addition programme. Since April 2023, 21 GW of thermal power capacity has been commissioned, while 48 GW, including 4.8 GW of stressed projects, is under construction. Contracts have also been awarded for another 16 GW of coal- and lignite-based capacity.On the renewable side, 148 GW of capacity is under construction, while another 48 GW is at various stages of planning and targeted for completion by 2029-30.The ministry said Indiaâs installed power generation capacity is projected to reach 874 GW by 2031-32, with states preparing 10-year resource adequacy plans to ensure generation capacity remains ahead of projected demand.

World.title: NHAI wins major arbitration, Rs 3,177-cr claim cut to Rs 46 cr
World.content:
The NHAIâs wins major arbitration case

NEW DELHI: NHAI, in a recent arbitration case, has got an arbitration order in its favour, rejecting the majority of claims â against the claim of Rs 3,177 crore by a contractor; the arbitral tribunal awarded only Rs 46 crore to settle the case.In an official statement, the highways authority said that the arbitration case involved 151-km Bareilly-Sitapur BOT (Toll) highway project in Uttar Pradesh.The dispute arose after NHAI terminated the concession agreement with Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL), a company promoted by Era Infra Engineering Ltd, in May 2019. The concessionaire had sought compensation of around Rs 3,177 crore through 30 claims before a three-member arbitral tribunal.In its award, the tribunal allowed only three claims worth about Rs 46 crore, along with applicable interest, while rejecting the overwhelming majority of the claims. The tribunal also upheld the validity of the âsupplementary agreementâ signed on March 30, 2015, and ruled that delays in the project were concurrent, weakening the concessionaire's case.NHAI had filed counterclaims relating to financial losses and public inconvenience caused by the stalled project.Although these counterclaims were not accepted, the authority successfully defended itself against the bulk of the concessionaire's claims, substantially reducing its potential financial exposure.The latest ruling adds to a series of arbitration successes for NHAI this year. In June, it secured an award of Rs 1,202 crore in the Tumkur-Chitradurga six-laning project in Karnataka. Earlier, arbitration in the Panipat-Jalandhar highway project involving claims exceeding Rs 8,000 crore was settled at Rs 819.96 crore in NHAI's favour. In another case relating to the Kamrej-Chalthan section of NH-48 in Gujarat, claims of Rs 174.5 crore were reduced to just Rs 54 lakh.toied

World.title: Follow example of Dharmendra Pradhan, resign from post, Naveen to Odisha Education Minister
World.content:
Former Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik on Monday (July 27, 2026) urged School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond to follow the example of former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and resign over errors in school textbooks for Classes I to VIII.

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Patnaik said the Biju Janata Dal (BJD) had been demanding Mr. Gond’s resignation for the past two to three weeks over the inaccuracies in the textbooks.

The Mohan Majhi government has faced significant public embarrassment following the detection of 1,678 mistakes in school textbooks printed for the 2026–27 academic session. Despite the errors being flagged and a high-level committee headed by Development Commissioner D.K. Singh being constituted, students continue to study from error-ridden books in classrooms.

At a press conference in Bhubaneswar on Monday (July 27, 2026), BJD spokesperson Lenin Mohanty reiterated the party’s demand for the Minister’s resignation, citing the widespread errors in textbooks for Classes I to VIII across Odisha.

The regional party also raised concerns over repeated question paper leak incidents. It stressed that preventing such occurrences and ensuring accountability required strict, impartial, and effective enforcement of the law.

“In Odisha, the BJP government passed the Odisha Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill, 2024 in the State Legislative Assembly on December 6, 2024. However, despite 23 question paper leak incidents coming to light over the past two years under the ‘double-engine’ government, not a single person has been punished in connection with these cases,” Mr. Mohanty said.

He added that the situation demonstrated that merely enacting stringent laws was insufficient, and that sincere implementation along with exemplary action against those responsible was urgently needed.

World.title: Activist demands time-bound prosecution in long-pending paper leak cases relating to two NDA MLAs in U.P.
World.content:
LAmid nationwide uproar over paper leaks, Lucknow-based social activist Amitabh Thakur on Monday (July 27, 2026) wrote to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath requesting effective, impartial and time-bound prosecution in the long-pending paper leak cases relating to Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) MLA Bedi Ram and Nishad Party MLA Vipul Dubey, both allies of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh.

“In the light of the nationwide concern over recent paper leak incidents and the declared zero-tolerance policy of both the Union and Uttar Pradesh Governments, older pending cases should also receive the same degree of seriousness and administrative attention. In the representation, I referred to the pending Railway Recruitment examination paper leak case of 2006, pending against Bedi Ram, Vipul Dubey and others for the last 20 years. Similarly, other criminal cases relating to examination paper leaks are also reported to be pending against Bedi Ram in different jurisdictions. The affidavits filed by both the MLAs to the Election Commission mention in detail the pending cases. I request the State government to ensure regular high-level review, effective representation by competent public prosecutors and continuous monitoring of these cases so that the judicial process proceeds in accordance with law without avoidable delay,” Mr. Thakur, a 1992-batch retired Indian Police Service (IPS) officer from the Uttar Pradesh cadre who leads Azad Adhikar Sena, an outfit, told The Hindu.

Mr. Ram, the SBSP MLA, is charged with six cases in Uttar Pradesh, two in Madhya Pradesh and one in Rajasthan. The charges against him include Sections 4/6 of the Rajasthan Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 1992: Unauthorised possession or disclosure of question paper, Sections 2/3 of the UP-Gangster Act, 1986: Punishment for a public servant, who illegally helps or supports a gang member before or after commission of crime, Sections 4/5/10 of the Uttar Pradesh Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 1998: Unauthorised possession, disclosure of question paper, leakage by person entrusted with examination work and penalties for both and Sections 3/9 of the Uttar Pradesh Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 1998: Use of unfair means and resources.

Mr. Dubey, also faces charges related to Railway Examination paper leak.

World.title: Woman who stopped Mumbai police van files complaint against online abuse
World.content:
Rhiya Yadav, also known as Rhiya Ahir, approached the MIDC Police station in Mumbai on Monday (July 27, 2026) regarding alleged cyberbullying and trolling. Last week, Ms. Rhiya had stopped a police van during a CJP protest in the city.

“I had earlier registered an online complaint on the cyber police department’s portal. Today, I sat with the police for the whole day to get the complaint registered,” she told The Hindu. She alleged that she was being bullied and stalked. She also complained of uncalled-for sexting. “There is an effort to spread hate against me online. They are slut-shaming me. This is abuse,” she said, adding that she did not want her family to get affected due to it.

The police said they had taken her statement and were examining the complaint.

World.title: Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur gets interim relief in demolition issue
World.content:
Moradabad Divisional Commissioner’s court on Monday (July 27, 2026) stayed the proposed demolition of 38 buildings at Mohammad Ali Jauhar University until the final hearing. The interim relief was granted after the university’s legal team moved an application to the Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Kumar Singh.

Earlier, Rampur Development Authority (RDA) on July 15 issued a demolition notice for 38 of 40 buildings at Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, linked to the SP leader Azam Khan, describing these structures as constructed without permission. The RDA gave 15 days’ time to the University to remove the “unauthorised” construction, adding the administration will proceed with the demolition if the institution fails to comply. The order was issued by the RDA vice-chairperson and Rampur District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi under Section 27 of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Planning and Development Act, 1973. Mr. Khan is the chairperson of Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, which runs the University.

World.title: Rajya Sabha adjourned again; Opposition MPs seek apology from Amit Shah
World.content:
The Rajya Sabha adjourned for the day on Monday (July 27, 2026) for the sixth day in the monsoon session without taking up any business. The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was listed for consideration and passing. But it could not be taken up as the Opposition demanded an apology from Union Home Minister Amit Shah for the police action against protesting students.

In the afternoon, when the House met at 2 p.m., Deputy Speaker Harivansh invited Minister of State for Home Nitayanand Rai to move the bill that provides the status of National Anthem for National Song. Opposition members Pramod Tiwari, John Brittas and Tiruchi Siva raised objections. While Mr. Tiwari and Mr. Brittas demanded a discussion on police atrocities, Mr. Siva said the Bill was against the Constitution.

The Deputy Chairman, however, denied the “point of order” raised by the members and Mr. Rai moved the Bill for consideration of the House amid din. Opposition members were heard shouting slogans demanding that Mr. Shah must come to the House and apologise for police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak. Mr. Harivansh adjourned the House till 3 p.m.

‘Youth are watching’

At 3 p.m. too, protests continued and the House was adjourned till 5.15 p.m.

At 5.15 p.m., the Deputy Chairman invited Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju. He said the government was ready for discussions on the issue of paper leaks and requested the Congress to take up the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, for discussion. “Such an important Bill has been brought forward. We appealed to the Congress yesterday, we have been appealing to them since this morning, but they are not agreeing,” he said, adding that the Congress claimed outside the House that no debates were allowed in Parliament. “We are requesting them to take up the discussion,” Mr. Rijiju added. “What kind of a method is this? We fold our hands and request you to speak, but you do not allow us to speak,” he said.

“Please do not do this. The youth of the country are watching. Everyone wants to hear the discussion on this Bill. If you (the Opposition) behave like this, then you will be punished. We have given assurance to the youth that we will discuss (the Bill). The Prime Minister took such a step, and you are not allowing us to discuss it. This is not right. I condemn this,” Mr. Rijiju said.

Countering this, Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge said the Opposition did not shy away from discussion. “But before discussion, the Home Minister should come and make a statement,” he said. When Mr. Kharge was speaking, BJP members raised their voices, and soon after that the House got adjourned for the day.

Earlier during the day, the Upper House witnessed two adjournments at 11 a.m. and 12 p.m. The Opposition had moved several adjournment motions under Rule 267, and Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan disallowed them. The Opposition members raised protests, forcing the Chairman to adjourn the House. “It has never happened in the history of India that boys were beaten... and they were gagged by pellets,” Mr. Kharge said in the morning.

World.title: ‘Gen Z’ protests test the Sangh, raise uncomfortable questions
World.content:
Protests by students over the alleged NEET paper leak appear to have hit closer to home for the BJP and the larger Sangh Parivar than previous agitations against the NDA government at the Centre.

After reports emerged that the daughter of Assam Revenue Minister Keshab Mahanta, Dibisa Mahanta, had joined the protests by students, other instances of disquiet among BJP members and those associated with the Sangh Parivar have also come to the fore.

News about Manika Rana, former president of the BJP’s youth wing in Uttarakhand’s Tehri Garhwal, also went viral on social media. Reports claimed that she had been expelled from the party after participating in the CJP- led student protest at Jantar Mantar.

Speaking to The Hindu, Ms. Rana confirmed that she had been to the protest on multiple occasions and that she supported the students’ demands. The youth leader, however, denied reports that she had been expelled because of her participation.

“I was removed from the post of youth wing president in April this year as I was busy due to certain personal engagements. Yes, I support all demands made by students, including the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan but I am still with the party and in touch with senior leaders,” she added.

Former Union Minister Dr. Murli Manohar Joshi had already expressed concerns over the police action against protesters on July 20, and after Mr. Pradhan’s resignation, he posted on X, “Better late than never”.

RSS member Ratan Sharda, who is also a contributor to the RSS mouthpiece Organiser, has publicly argued that the BJP’s communication machinery and IT Cell failed to effectively counter the narrative around the CJP-led “Cockroach Protests”, calling it a “spectacular failure”.

In a post on X, which he clarified as “his own view” and had “nothing to do with the RSS”, Mr. Sharda said the BJP’s media team relied on memes and “whataboutery” instead of building a counter-narrative, and failed to gauge growing youth anger over issues such as NEET, lacking a feedback mechanism from the ground.

He added that Prime Minister Narendra Modi having to personally intervene to regain the narrative reflected poorly on the party’s communication strategy, while asserting that his criticism was intended to strengthen, not undermine, nationalist forces.

For the BJP and the RSS, the protests have raised uncomfortable questions over a support base they have long taken for granted and troubles at home.

World.title: Delhi Police step up drive to take down posts on protests
World.content:
The Delhi Police is in the process of sending takedown notices to Instagram, in an attempt to remove several reels and posts that emerged during the youth protests at Jantar Mantar and elsewhere, officials said. A senior police officer said they regularly flag offensive social media posts with the concerned authorities for removal.

Also read | Calm returns to Jantar Mantar after 36-day NEET protest ends; Dipke, Wangchuk recuperate

Without specifying the time frame or the nature of the content, the officer admitted that a large number of such posts had recently been flagged and taken down. He also said that more than 400 social media accounts operating from outside the country and posting offensive content had been blocked. The police had previously mentioned those 400 accounts in a press conference.

“We do not maintain the number of offensive posts because they are too many. It is an ongoing process. There is a dedicated social media team that continuously monitors such posts, and sometimes they are also flagged by other agencies. We do not keep a count,” the officer said.

Several users posted details of posts that were taken down by Meta in response to a legal demand by the government. It is unclear how many government organisations are sending takedown notices to Instagram on protest-related content. While former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation settled the protests’ main demand, government officials have expressed frustration with the way the demonstrations and support were amplified on social media, mainly on Instagram.

Of the removed posts reviewed by The Hindu, many featured police violence against the students, or criticism thereof, on July 20, 2026, when police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)’s Rapid Action Force in and around Jantar Mantar used lathis, tear gas rounds, and pellet guns on protesters.

Law enforcement agencies typically send takedown notices under Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act that notify platforms of specified content that is illegal, however without a legally binding takedown requirement. Meta, however, in recent months has acted to comply with nearly every single 79(3)(b) request “automatically,” potentially handing authorities powers of instant censorship.

A Meta spokesperson did not respond to questions on the scale of the takedown orders they are currently receiving from authorities in India, and what they are doing in response to those requests.

“The Internet Freedom Foundation condemns this takedown drive and calls for the notices to be disclosed and withdrawn,” the Delhi-based digital rights advocacy group said in a statement. “On the reports available, the content being removed is political expression. The movement at Jantar Mantar has been conducted as much through reels, memes, posters and digital artwork as through assembly on the ground. This is how a digital native generation raised online speaks about accountability.”

“Unpublished directions are also contrary to [the Supreme Court’s guidelines laid out in] Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, which requires that orders restricting fundamental rights be published so that they can be challenged,” IFF added. “If the underlying theory is defamation of the Prime Minister, the police have no role at all. Defamation under Section 356 of the BNS is a non-cognizable offence, prosecuted only on a complaint by the person aggrieved under Section 222 of the BNSS.”

World.title: Bihar policeman who fired AK-47 at protesters suspended; viral video triggers political storm
World.content:
The viral video of a Bihar policeman firing an AK-47 rifle during protests in Siwan triggered a political storm in Parliament on Monday (July 27, 2026), with Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi demanding an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and action against those who “attacked” students.

The policeman has been suspended and a departmental inquiry ordered, Superintendent of Police (SP) of Siwan district Puran Kumar Jha said.

At least three protesters sustained gunshot injuries and were admitted to a private hospital in Patna, where their condition is stated to be stable. One of them was discharged on July 27.

In a post in Hindi on X, Mr. Gandhi said “the entire system is downright murderous against students”.

“Reports are coming in that AK-47s have been fired at protesting students in Bihar, and hundreds have been arrested and booked under FIRs. Modi ji, what happened to your promise that no FIRs would be filed against students and that they would be released? Instead, they are being subjected to deadly attacks and brutality,” he said.

“Pellet guns were used against students in Delhi, and AK-47s in Bihar. Whether it is Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, or Delhi — the pattern is the same everywhere. This government is dishonest. Reform is beyond its capability. It will renege on its promises and use every tactic to suppress the students’ voices,” Mr. Gandhi added.

Several Congress leaders also condemned the reported use of force. Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal demanded an explanation from Union Home Minister Amit Shah, asking who had ordered the use of AK-47s in Bihar and pellet guns in Delhi. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra questioned the deployment of such weapons against protesters, saying, “The students are not terrorists.” Congress MP Manish Tewari termed the reported action against unarmed students “barbaric, inhuman, and an atrocity” and said the use of excessive force violated established procedures for handling protests.

Posting the video on social media, Leader of the Opposition in the Bihar Assembly and Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Yadav, whose elder brother Tej Pratap Yadav was arrested on July 26, demanded action against the officials responsible. He warned that if the arrested students and his brother were not released within 24 hours, the party would launch a massive statewide agitation.

The video of the policeman firing the AK-47 has circulated widely on social media since July 26. “The video surfaced late because Internet services remained suspended for 24 hours after the protest,” a local journalist in Siwan told The Hindu.

Departmental probe

The policeman has been identified as Abhishek Kumar, attached to the District Intelligence Unit. “The policeman has been suspended and a departmental inquiry ordered,” Siwan SP Mr. Jha said. Asked who had authorised the firing, Mr. Jha said the matter would be examined in the departmental probe.

According to a police statement, the officer fired four rounds in the air near J.P. Chowk to protect government property and lives, and no one was injured in that firing. The three injured protesters — a 17-year-old (name withheld), Aakash Kumar (22) and Bullet Kumar Gond (20) — sustained gunshot wounds at locations away from J.P. Chowk. They were shifted from Siwan Sadar Hospital to a private hospital in Patna after initial treatment. Police have also registered an FIR against the three.

Police said 694 people were detained during the July 25 protests, including 339 minors who were later released after verification. Ninety-one policemen and 13 civilians were injured, while 14 police vehicles were damaged. Two Block Development Officers sustained grievous injuries, the police said.

The violence erupted during a Bihar bandh called by the All India Students Association. Police said protesters pelted stones at security personnel in Siwan before the armed officer opened fire. Demonstrations were reported across Bihar, including in Patna, where police vehicles were vandalised and several protesters were detained.

World.title: Sharmila Dhankar wins gold, Shilpa Shyla bronze in para shot put at CWG 2026
World.content:
Para-athlete Sharmila Dhankar clinched India’s second gold medal in this edition of the Commonwealth Games in the Women’s Shot Put F57 Final. Shipla Shyla, the other medallist in the event walked away with bronze with a personal best throw of 7.26m.

Sharmila, who was born in a zamindar family in Haryana’s Chhithroli, ended India’s 20-year wait for a Para Athletics medal at the Commonwealth Games with a season-best throw of 9.81m. She also became India’s first-ever CWG Gold medallist in Para Athletics and the first Indian woman to win a Para Athletics medal at the Games.

India has now won two medals in the same Para Athletics event for the first time at the CWG.

World.title: Ajaya Babu wins silver, India’s 6th weightlifting medal at 2026 CWG
World.content:
Ajaya Babu lifted a total of 330kg to win silver in men’s 79kg weightlifting. Ajaya lifted 149kg in snatch and then 181kg in clean and jerk. Malaysia’s Erry Hidayat Muhammad won gold with a total lift of 331kg, which was a Games record. England’s Chris Murray won bronze after heaving 325kg. Hailing from Andhra Pradesh’s Vizianagram district, Ajaya Babu lifted a Games record 149kg in snatch and 181kg in clean and jerk for a total of 330kg to win the second prize, narrowly missing out on gold to Malaysia’s Erry Hidayat Muhammad, who totalled a Games record 331kg (147 + 184) during a gripping contest on Monday night.



This was India’s sixth medal in weightlifting in the current edition of the Games. Rishikanta Singh opened the account first with a silver medal before Mirabai Chanu won her third consecutive CWG gold. Ayaya’s silver is the third weightlifting medal for India on Monday alone, with Gyaneshwari Yadav having won silver and Bindyarani Devi winning bronze earlier in the day.

First, Hidayat lifted 181kg to smash the Games record, the Indian then bettered it within seconds by lifting 181kg in his final attempt to break the record again for 330kg. Hidayat did one better, breaking the record again with a lift of 184kg in his final attempt to win the gold medal.

Earlier, after a failed second attempt at 149kg, Ajaya Babu made a fine comeback to lift the weight in his final try and set a new Games record, finishing at the top of the heap at the end of snatch section ahead of England’s Chris Murray (148kg) and Malaysia’s Erry Hidayat Muhammad (147kg).

He had 145kg listed as his first attempt and nailed it too easily. Entering the clean and jerk section on a high, Ajaya Babu looked confident of winning the top prize but his opponent from Malaysia edged the Indian out eventually.



Seen as one of India’s fastest-growing lifters, Ajaya Babu had in the past won the gold medal in the men’s 79kg category at the 2025 Commonwealth Championships in Ahmedabad with a personal-best total lift of 335kg (152kg snatch + 183kg clean & jerk), breaking the championship records. That performance earned him his direct qualification spot for Glasgow 2026.

World.title: Ministry pushing RBI to open licences for more urban cooperative banks: Secretary Ashish Kumar Bhutani
World.content:
Of the 1,450 UCBs in the country, almost 1,100 are in three states — Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Karnataka.

The Ministry of Cooperation has urged the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to open licences for more urban cooperative banks in the country, a top official said on Monday.

Speaking at a book release function, Cooperation Ministry Secretary Ashish Kumar Bhutani said that India needs urban cooperative banks (UCBs) in every town of the country.

Echoing the views, Satish K Marathe, director, Central Board of RBI, said there are hundreds of districts in the country that do not have UCBs.

“Of the 1,450 UCBs in the country, almost 1,100 are in three states — Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Karnataka. The rest of the country has very few (urban cooperative) banks,” Marathe said, speaking after the release of the book ‘Cooperative Management: The Indian Perspective’, co-authored by KK Tripathy, Joint Secretary in the Economic Advisory Council to The Prime Minister. Harekrishna Misra and SK Wadkar co-wrote the book.

World.title: Commonwealth Games: Sarvesh Kushare bags silver in high jump
World.content:
Indian national record holder Sarvesh Anil Kushare jumped 2.25m to win the men’s high jump silver medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow on Monday.

This is his first major multi-sporting medal as he bettered the bronze medal won by his compatriot Tejaswin Shankar in the last edition.

Sarvesh, who cleared 2.31m last month at Inter State Athletics Championships to create a new national record, cleared the 2.25m mark in his final attempt but failed to clear the 2.28m in three attempts.



His opponent Romaine Beckford failed to clear the 2.28m mark in three attempts but won the gold by the virtue of clearing the 2.25m mark at once.

World.title: India at CWG 2026 Day 6 Schedule: Full list of Indian athletes in action on Tuesday
World.content:
Weightlifter Gyaneshwari Yadav spearheaded India’s campaign with a silver medal in the women’s 53kg event, while Bindyarani Devi added a bronze, as the country’s track and field athletes and boxers advanced to the finals and quarterfinals respectively at the Commonwealth Games on Monday.

In athletics, M Sreeshankar comfortably booked his place in the men’s long jump final after clearing the automatic qualification standard of 8m with an effortless opening leap of 8.01m in Group A. Compatriot Lokesh Sathyanathan also progressed after a best effort of 7.77m earned him a place among the top-12 performers across both groups.

Indian boxing also enjoyed a productive day as former world youth champion Sachin Siwach and youngster Ankush entered the quarterfinals of the men’s 60kg and 80kg events respectively, moving within one victory of assured medals.

There was disappointment, however, in the men’s 100m, where national record holder Gurindervir Singh failed to progress beyond the heats. The 25-year-old clocked 10.39 seconds to finish second in his heat behind Jamaica’s Rohan Watson but ended up only 28th overall, well outside the qualification places.

World.title: Dimple Kapadia’s ‘forever’ story with Rajesh Khanna sparks conversation on lasting love
World.content:
Dimple Kapadia once fondly spoke about her first meeting with her late husband and actor Rajesh Khanna. “This was after I signed Bobby. We were going to Ahmedabad on a private flight. There was a function there which he had to attend. And I, being a Gujarati, was invited too. I was born a drama queen. He was sitting next to me. I told him…there will be a lot of crowd…will you hold my hand? He said, yes, of course. So, I said, “Forever”? (Laughs),” Kapadia once disclosed in an interview with FICCI FLO Jaipur Chapter in 2018.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

Reflecting on the actor’s candid admission, Delnna Rrajesh, psychotherapist and relationship breakthrough coach, called it a light-hearted moment, adding, “yet it captures something deeply human.” “Most of us enter love hoping that forever is possible. Very few people walk into a marriage expecting separation or heartbreak. We fall in love not just with a person but with a future we begin creating in our minds. We imagine growing old together, celebrating milestones, raising children, travelling, building a home and sharing life’s ordinary moments. Love is not only about the present. It is also about the future we dare to dream,” shared Delnna.



Here’s what you should consider (Photo: Freepik) Here’s what you should consider (Photo: Freepik)

This is why the beginning of a relationship feels so magical. “During this phase, our brains are flooded with chemicals such as dopamine and oxytocin that increase excitement, attachment and optimism. However, lasting love is not built on chemistry alone. The butterflies eventually settle, but what remains is something much deeper. Healthy relationships survive not because two people never change, but because they continue choosing each other as they change,” expressed Delnna.

One of the biggest misconceptions about finding “the one” is that compatibility is something people either have or don’t have. According to Delnna, strong attraction, chemistry, and excitement are beautiful beginnings, but they should also be accompanied by curiosity. “Does this person take responsibility for their actions? Can they apologise sincerely? Do they respect your boundaries? Are they emotionally available during difficult times? Do your values align? Can you both handle disagreements without attacking each other’s character? These questions often predict the health of a relationship far better than intense emotions alone.”



Relationships become stronger not because difficult conversations are avoided but because they are approached with honesty, respect, and compassion.

What helps?

While there is no perfect formula, certain habits consistently strengthen long-term relationships:

*Stay curious about your partner even after years together. People continue evolving throughout life.

*Learn to repair conflicts quickly rather than trying to win every argument.

Express appreciation regularly instead of assuming your partner already knows.

*Protect respect during disagreements. Anger may pass, but hurtful words often remain.

*Continue creating new memories together instead of living only through old ones.

*Choose emotional honesty over emotional perfection. Healthy couples are not those who never struggle. They are the ones who know how to reconnect after they do.

Some relationships last a lifetime. Some do not. But every healthy relationship teaches us something about love, resilience, ourselves and what truly matters. “The dream of ‘forever’ is beautiful, but perhaps the real secret is learning to make each ordinary day worthy of that promise,” said Delnna.



DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

World.title: Egypt conquered, Asia next: Anahat Singh plots her route to direct LA28 spot
World.content:
Anahat Singh can’t wait to meet her cousins when she returns home. It’s the only way she feels she could make sense of the past few days. That, and catching the new Spiderman movie releasing at the end of the month.

The 18-year-old, in her fifth and final attempt, won the squash Junior World Championship, a feat that ended 16 years of Egyptian dominance in the event, and landed a first-ever singles squash world title for a country that has produced world-level talent, but not quite like the teenager from Delhi.

“I don’t think I’ve really had time to just sit down and actually understand what happened or exactly how it happened. I don’t think it’s going to sink in until I’m actually back home with my friends and family, and talking to them about it,” Anahat told The Indian Express from Canada.

The word ‘pressure’ being used by her repeatedly is a mark of the load of expectations being carried by the 18-year-old. Ranked 20th in the world, there is a genuine sense in the country that she could be a world-beater in her sport as the performances in the senior circuit start to improve, and the tour titles arrive.

In a way, this Junior World Championship was a farewell of sorts for her and a ‘welcome to the big league’ moment. Part of that is also her reluctance to be overawed by the might of the Egyptians, who have dominated the sport. Their presence is not a cause of worry for her.



“The way they’ve been brought up since they’ve been kids, for them, it’s like cricket for India. They’ve been brought up hearing about it, looking at squash all the time, playing squash all the time. I was there in Egypt a year ago for the World Juniors and kids almost five years old would be playing from 6 am. I would see them at 11 pm at the squash courts with coaches, and there were 15 different courts around the whole complex,” explained Anahat.

Beating the assembly line of Egyptians and their ability to go deep in tournaments requires her to level up physically. In big–ticket tournament with 6-7 games for a chance at a medal, working on her overall fitness – and muscle mass in particular – is something Anahat is looking at.



“I’m not amazing in the physicality aspect of it. I’m focusing on that right now. Muscle mass is definitely something that I’m working on improving. Going to the gym a little bit more and focusing on the strength aspect, that’s something that can really improve my game a lot more,” she said.

In a previous press interaction facilitated by the Sports Authority of India, Anahat had said, “Just learning how to stick with the top players and being able to back up multiple tough matches continuously – not just playing one good match and going flat in the next – that’s really important, especially in platinum events, since they’re quite long. You have to play almost six or seven matches just to reach the finals.”



Olympic dreams

The JSW athlete will have multiple pathways to reach the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where squash will make its debut. But a gold medal at this year’s Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya offers the clearest route. But along that path are some high-ranked opponents, ones whom the Indian is relishing the idea of taking on.

“There are so many top players who are playing this event, like Sivasangari Subramaniam and Satomi Watanabe, number six and number seven in the world respectively. I’ve played them multiple times and always had close games. I’m just really looking forward to playing against them again,” said Anahat, adding, “The stakes are, of course, very, very different now.”

Anahat won Asian Games team and mixed medals at Hangzhou, but this will be the first time she enters the tournament with a clear shot at a title charge. A gold medal gives her a direct entry into the LA Games, but crucially will aso allow her to put in a two-year focused programme built solely towards squash’s bow at the Olympics.



“It’s just that if I get it in this way, it would be amazing. I can just spend the next two years training towards the Olympics rather than trying to qualify for it,” she added.
